body.text: Mahāsāhasrapramardanī
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī</s>

body.text: namo bhagavatyai āryamahāsāhasrapramardanyai //
body.translated_text: Homage to the Blessed <s>Āryamahāsāhasrapramardanī</s>!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma / gṛdhrakūṭe parvate dakṣiṇe pārśve buddhagocare ratnavṛkṣe prabhāse vanaṣaṇḍe mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdham ardhatrayodaśabhir bhikṣuśataiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, on the southern slope, in the radiant grove of jewel-trees in the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>—twelve hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s>.

body.text: tadyathā / āyuṣmatā ca śāriputreṇa / āyuṣmatā ca mahāmaudgalyāyanena / āyuṣmatā ca mahākāśyapena / ayuṣmatā ca gayākāśyapena / āyuṣmatā ca nadīkāśyapena / āyuṣmatā coruvilvākāśyapena / āyuṣmatā cājñātakauṇḍinyena / āyuṣmatā ca mahākātyāyanena / āyuṣmatā ca vakulena / āyuṣmatā ca vāṣpeṇa / āyuṣmatā ca koṣṭhilena / āyuṣmatā ca vāgīśena / āyuṣmatā cāśvajitā / āyuṣmatā ca subhūtinā / āyuṣmatā ca suvāhunā / āyuṣmatā cāniruddhena / āyuṣmatā ca revatena / āyuṣmatā ca nandikena / āyuṣmatā cānandena / evaṃ pramukhair ardhatrayodaśabhir bhikṣuśatais tasmiṃś ca samaye bhagavān sabhikṣusaṃgho māgadhena rājñājātaśatruṇā vaidehīputreṇa satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito 'rcito yācayitaś cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ //
body.translated_text: Namely: the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Nadīkāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Uruvilvākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Vakula</s>, the venerable <s>Vāṣpa</s>, the venerable <s>Koṣṭhila</s>, the venerable <s>Vāgīśa</s>, the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the venerable <s>Suvāhu</s>, the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, the venerable <s>Revata</s>, the venerable <s>Nandika</s>, and the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>—with these and other leaders, twelve hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s> in all. And at that time the Blessed One, together with the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, was honored, respected, esteemed, worshipped, revered, and provided with robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick by <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, king of <s>Magadha</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>.

body.text: tena khalu samayena vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ mahān bhūmicālo 'bhūd abhrakūṭaṃ ca prādurbhūtam / mahati cākālavātāśanir mahāmeghaś ca samutthito devo garjati guḍaguḍāyati vidyutaś ca niścaranti / daśadiśaś cākulībhūtāś tamo 'ndhakāraṃ ca prādurbhūtam / nakṣatrāṇi ca na bhāṣante / candrasūryau na prabhavato na tapato na virocato na ca prabhāsvarau bhavataḥ //
body.translated_text: At that time, in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, there occurred a great earthquake, and a mass of clouds appeared. A great untimely storm of wind and lightning arose, and a great cloud formed. The sky thundered and rumbled, and lightning-bolts flashed forth. The ten directions were thrown into confusion, and darkness appeared. The stars did not shine. The sun and moon had no power, gave no heat, shed no light, and were not radiant.

body.text: atha bhagavān adrākṣīd divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakena vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ tāni bhayāni prādurbhūtani /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One saw with his divine eye—purified and surpassing human vision—that those terrors had arisen in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>.

body.text: apy ekatyānāṃ vaiśālakānāṃ licchavīnāṃ yā grāmāntaḥ purīṣābhūtair adhiṣṭhitā abhisaṃsṛṣṭā / apy ekatyānāṃ ca grāmakumārakānāṃ gaṇakamahāmātyāmātyāpārṣadyādāsīdāsakarmakarapreṣyaparicārakāḥ bhūtair abhibhūtāḥ samantataś ca vaiśālījanapade yā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā bhītās trastāḥ saṃvignāḥ saṃdṛṣṭaromakūpajātā ūrdhvamukhāḥ prakrandanto buddhadharmasaṃghān namasyanti //
body.translated_text: Some of the <s>Vaiśālika Licchavīs</s> had their homes possessed and afflicted by spirits that had become like filth in their villages. And some village boys, as well as the accountants, great ministers, ministers, assembly-members, female and male servants, workers, messengers, and attendants were overpowered by spirits. And throughout the <s>Vaiśālī</s> territory, the <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, and <s>upāsikās</s>—frightened, terrified, alarmed, their hair standing on end—with faces raised, crying out, paid homage to the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>.

body.text: ye ca brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo buddhaśāsane nābhipannās te cāpy ekatyā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo brāhmaṇaṃ namasyanti / kecit punaḥ śakraṃ kecil lokapālān namasyanti / kecit punar maheśvaramāṇibhadrapūrṇabhadrahārītīcandrasūryagrahanakṣatraparvatavanaṣaṇḍauṣadhivṛkṣanadyutsasarohradakūpataḍāgacaityasthānāny api namasyanti /
body.translated_text: And those Brahmins and householders who had not entered the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching—some of those Brahmins and householders paid homage to <s>Brahman</s>; some paid homage to <s>Śakra</s>; some to the <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Guardians); and some paid homage to <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Māṇibhadra</s>, <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s>, <s>Hārītī</s>, the sun, the moon, the planets, the constellations, mountains, groves, medicinal herbs, trees, rivers, springs, lakes, pools, wells, ponds, and sacred sites.

body.text: kathaṃ nāmaitad syād vayam evaṃrūpād upadravato bhayasthānāt parimucyema iti //
body.translated_text: "How might we be freed from such a calamity and place of fear?"

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tathā rūpam ṛddhyabhisaṃskāram akāśīd yathā rūpeṇa ṛddhyabhisaṃskāreṇābhisaṃskṛtena trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ svareṇa vijñāpya sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokaṃ prasādya sa sannipātayām āsa / atha brahmā sahāpatir brahmakāyikāś ca devāḥ śakraś ca devānām indro devāś ca trayastriṃśāś catvāraś ca mahārājānaś caturmahārājakāyikāś ca devā aṣṭāviṃśatiś ca mahāyakṣasenāpatayo dvātriṃśac ca mahāyakṣanagnā hārītī ca saputrikā saparivārā atikrāntavarṇā atikrāntāyāṃ rātrau kevalaṃ kalyaṃ gṛdhrakūṭaṃ parvataṃ svakena varṇānubhāvenodāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte sthitā ekavāgekasvaraikapadena bhagavantaṃ gāthābhir abhituṣṭuvuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One performed such a feat of miraculous power that by that feat of miraculous power, having made the great trichiliocosm aware through his voice and having gladdened the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, he caused them all to assemble. Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> and the gods of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> realm, <s>Śakra</s> the lord of the gods, the gods of the <s>Trayastriṃśa</s> heaven, the four Great Kings and the gods of the <s>Caturmahārājakāyika</s> realm, twenty-eight great <s>yakṣa</s> generals, thirty-two great <s>yakṣa</s> chiefs, and <s>Hārītī</s> with her children and retinue—of surpassing beauty—in the last part of the night, at early dawn, having illuminated <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain with their own splendor and brilliant radiance, approached the Blessed One. Having approached and bowed their heads at the Blessed One's feet, standing to one side, they praised the Blessed One with verses in a single voice, a single tone, and a single word:

children.translated_text: "Blazing with the radiance of gold, luminous as the full moon,
like glorious <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, a mine of heroic jewels to behold,

body.text: siṃhavāraṇavikrāntamattanāgaparākramaḥ /
body.translated_text: with the prowess of a lion and a bull-elephant, the valor of a maddened <s>nāga</s>,

body.text: parvato vā suvarṇasya niṣkaṃ jambūnadasya vā //
body.translated_text: like a mountain of gold, or a coin of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold,

body.text: candro vā vimale vyomni nakṣatrebhiḥ puraskṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text: or like the moon in a spotless sky, attended by the constellations,

body.text: madhye śrāvakasaṃghasya lakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text: adorned with the marks [of a great being] amidst the assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s>,

children.text: lokaḥ sadevako hy eṣa muniṃ śaraṇam āgataḥ /
children.translated_text: this world with its gods has come to the Sage for refuge;
for the benefit of humankind, the time of protection has arrived.
The <s>Sāhasrapramardana Sūtra</s>, proclaimed by all the <s>Buddhas</s>,
is the supreme boundary-binding extending to the <s>Cakravāḍa</s> (world-rim) mountains.

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottamam /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O Hero among Men! Homage to you, O Supreme among Men!
With palms joined we pay homage to the Dharma-King, the Great Sage."

body.text: atha bhagavān muhūrtaṃ tūṣṇībhavenādhivāsya caturo mahārājān āmantrayāmāsa //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having assented with a moment of silence, addressed the four Great Kings:

body.text: naitaṃ te mahārājānaḥ pratirūpaṃ bhaved yad yuṣmat pariṣado 'smat pariṣadaṃ viheṭhayitavyaṃ manyate / tat kasya hetoḥ / ito hi mānuṣe loke buddhotpādo dharmasvākhyātatā ca saṃghasupratipannatā ca / idam asmin bījam avaropya buddhā bhagavanto loka utpadyante / pratyekabuddhāś cārhantaḥ śrāvakāś cāsminn ime lokāḥ kuśalamūlāny avaropya sa daśato dvātriṃśatāṃ devanikāyānām anyatarānyatare devanikāye utpadyante / rājāno 'pi bhavanti caturaṅginaś caturdvīpeśvarāś cakravartinaḥ / samudraparyante mahāpṛthivīmaṇḍale dharmeṇa rājaṃ kārayanti / teṣāṃ ca putrasahasraṃ bhavati śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ mahānagnabalavegadhārināṃ parasainyapramardakānāṃ saptaratnasamanvāgatānām / tad yuṣmākam alpotsukavihāreṇa viharatām evaṃrūpāṇām asmin loke notpattir bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: "It is not fitting, O Great Kings, that your assemblies should think of harassing my assembly. For what reason? Because in this human world there is the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>, and the well-practiced <s>Saṃgha</s>. This is the seed planted here: the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> arise in the world. And <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s>—in these worlds, having planted roots of merit, they are born in one or another of the thirty-two classes of gods. They also become kings—possessors of the four divisions of the army, lords of the four continents, <s>Cakravartins</s> (universal sovereigns). They cause righteous rule to prevail over the great circle of the earth bounded by the ocean. And they have a thousand sons—brave, heroic, of excellent form, possessing great strength, speed, and power, crushers of enemy armies, endowed with the seven treasures. If you dwell in a state of little enthusiasm, such beings will no longer arise in this world."

body.text: atha vaiśramaṇo mahārājo 'bhyudgamyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ kṛtvā bhagavantam eva namasyamāno bhagavantam etad avocat // santi bhadanta bhagavann asmākam udārāṇi gṛhasthānabhavanāni nagarodyānavimānakūṭāgāraharmyaniryūhatoraṇagavākṣaśubharucitavividhavicitrapaṭṭadāmaghaṇṭācāmaramuktājālaparikṣiptāni
body.translated_text: Then the Great King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, rising from his seat, draping his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, paying homage to the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: "There are, Venerable Blessed One, our magnificent residences—palace-cities, garden-towers, mansions, upper chambers, terraces, gateways, windows, beautifully and variously adorned with canopies, bell-garlands, fly-whisks, and pearl-nets,

body.text: dhūpaghaṭikāni dhūpitāni puṣpāvakīrṇāni yeṣu vayaṃ nārīśatasahasraparivṛtāḥ saṃpūrṇaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāmaguṇaiḥ samarpitāḥ samanvaṅgībhūtā viharāmaḥ / teṣām asmākaṃ bhadanta bhagavan pramattānāṃ pramādavihāravihāriṇāṃ viharatāṃ pariṣadaḥ samantād daśadiśo 'nnapānabhojanāni mārgayanti / prapalāyamānāḥ strīpuruṣadārakadārikāṇāṃ tiryagjātagarbhānāṃ tiryagyonigatānām api ca prāṇinām ojo haranti viheṭhayanti vighnayanti mārayanti / jīvitād vyaparopayanti / te vayaṃ bhadanta bhagavato 'ntike caturvarṇāṃ pariṣadāṃ purataḥ svakasvakānāṃ pariṣadāṃ rūpalakṣaṇaṃ darśayiṣyāmaḥ / yasya pariṣado yo graho bhaviṣyati / tatas tasya mahārājasyodāracaityapratimā kartavyā / āturasya ca hastena tasya mahārājasya nāmnā nānāgandhadhūpā dhūpayitavyāḥ / puṣpāvakīrṇāṃ dhāraṇīṃ kṛtvā dīpāṃś cādīpya tatra caitye pūjā kartavyā / madīyāyāḥ pariṣado bhadanta bhagavan yakṣagrahagṛhītasya īdṛśaṃ rūpalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: with incense-burners, perfumed, strewn with flowers—where we dwell surrounded by hundreds of thousands of women, fully endowed with the five qualities of sensual pleasure. Yet, Venerable Blessed One, while we dwell heedlessly in the abode of heedlessness, our assemblies roam the ten directions in search of food and drink. Fleeing, they steal the vital essence of women, men, boys, girls, beings born from wombs of animals, and beings gone to animal realms; they harass them, obstruct them, kill them, and deprive them of life. Therefore, Venerable Blessed One, we shall display before the Blessed One, before the fourfold assembly, the form and characteristics of our respective assemblies' [spirit-possessions]. Whichever spirit belongs to whichever Great King's assembly—for that one, a noble image of that Great King's <s>caitya</s> (shrine) should be made. And by the hand of the afflicted person, various incenses should be burned in the name of that Great King. Having made a <s>dhāraṇī</s> strewn with flowers and having lit lamps, worship should be performed at that <s>caitya</s>. Venerable Blessed One, this is the form and characteristics of one seized by a <s>yakṣa</s>-spirit of my assembly:

children.translated_text: "He laughs, becomes frightened, frequently babbles incoherently and becomes agitated;

children.text: nidrā cāviśate tasya śūlo vāpy upajāyate //
children.translated_text: sleep overcomes him, and sharp pain arises.
He constantly gazes upward and pursues the constellations;

children.text: rātrau praharṣam āyāti vepate stanate sadā //
children.translated_text: at night he becomes excited, trembles, and always groans."

body.text: tatra mantrapadāny asti lokanātha śṛṇohi me //
body.translated_text: "For this, there are <s>mantra</s>-words—O World-Protector, hear me!"

body.text: syād yathedam //
body.translated_text: "Let it be thus:"

body.text: siddhe / susiddhe / satve are / araṇe / bale / mahābale / jambhe stambhe jaṭile / akhane / makhame / khakhane / kharaṭṭe / kharaṅge / haripiṅgale timiṅgile svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>siddhe / susiddhe / satve are / araṇe / bale / mahābale / jambhe stambhe jaṭile / akhane / makhame / khakhane / kharaṭṭe / kharaṅge / haripiṅgale timiṅgile svāhā</s>

body.text: sidhyantu me mantrapadāḥ svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca vaiśramaṇasya mahārājasya nāmnā balenaiśvaryādhipatyena ca svāhā //
body.translated_text: "May these <s>mantra</s>-words be efficacious! May there be well-being for me and all beings, by the name, power, sovereignty, and authority of Great King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>! <s>Svāhā</s>!"

body.text: atha dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārājo 'bhyudgamyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ kṛtvā bhagavantam eva namasyamāno bhagavantam
body.translated_text: Then the Great King <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, rising from his seat, draping his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, paying homage to the Blessed One, spoke

body.text: etad avocat / asmat pariṣado bhadanta bhagavan gandharvagrahagṛhītasya īdṛśaṃ rūpalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: thus to the Blessed One: "Venerable Blessed One, this is the form and characteristics of one seized by a <s>gandharva</s>-spirit of my assembly:

children.translated_text: "He dances and sings, is fond of ornaments,

children.text: alubdhaḥ satyavādi ca hasate kupyate punaḥ //
children.translated_text: is not greedy, speaks truth, laughs and then becomes angry.
He is overcome by craving, his eyes are red, fever constantly seizes him,

children.text: unmiṣati na cakṣuś ca śayate ca parāṅmukhaḥ //
children.translated_text: his eye does not open, and he sleeps facing away."

body.text: tatra mantrapadāny asti lokanātha śṛṇohi me //
body.translated_text: "For this, there are <s>mantra</s>-words—O World-Protector, hear me!"

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: "Let it be thus:"

body.text: akhe / nakhe / vinakhe / bandhe / varāṇe / capale / vakhe / vakhane / vakhiṇe / akhine / nakhine / vahale / bhage / bhagandare / vaśe vaśavartini / svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>akhe / nakhe / vinakhe / bandhe / varāṇe / capale / vakhe / vakhane / vakhiṇe / akhine / nakhine / vahale / bhage / bhagandare / vaśe vaśavartini / svāhā</s>

body.text: mucyantu sarvasatvāḥ sarvagrahebhyo dhṛtarāṣṭrasya mahārājasya nāmnā balenaiśvaryādhipatyena ca svāhā //
body.translated_text: "May all beings be freed from all spirits, by the name, power, sovereignty, and authority of Great King <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>! <s>Svāhā</s>!"

body.text: atha virūḍhako mahārājo 'bhyudgamyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ kṛtvā bhagavantam eva namasyamāno bhagavantam etad avocat / asmat pariṣado bhadanta bhagavan kumbhāṇḍagrahagṛhītasya īdṛśaṃ rūpalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Then the Great King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, rising from his seat, draping his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, paying homage to the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: "Venerable Blessed One, this is the form and characteristics of one seized by a <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s>-spirit of my assembly:

children.text: balavatī tṛṣā bhonti vibhrāntaś cāpi prekṣate /
children.translated_text: "There is powerful thirst, and he gazes about bewildered;

children.text: mukhaṃ lohitam ābhāti bhūmau svapiti kuñcitaḥ //
children.translated_text: his face appears red, and he sleeps on the ground curled up.
He is of foul complexion, with emaciated limbs, long hair and nails,

children.text: durgandho malinaś cāpi mṛśā sambhinnā bhāṣante //
children.translated_text: foul-smelling and dirty, and he speaks falsely and incoherently."

body.text: tatra mantrapadāny asti lokanātha śṛṇohi me //
body.translated_text: "For this, there are <s>mantra</s>-words—O World-Protector, hear me!"

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: "Let it be thus:"

body.text: khakhakhame / khalane / khalane / khalome / kharalikhe / kharakhe / khaṭine / kharali / karakhi / kaśane / karaṭe / kāle kāmini / vidhali / vidhiye / vidheye / śayane / samavate / śami śamini svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>khakhakhame / khalane / khalane / khalome / kharalikhe / kharakhe / khaṭine / kharali / karakhi / kaśane / karaṭe / kāle kāmini / vidhali / vidhiye / vidheye / śayane / samavate / śami śamini svāhā</s>

body.text: śāmyantu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvagrahāḥ sarvabhayopadravā virūḍhakasya mahārājasya nāmnā balenaiśvaryādhipatyena ca svāhā //
body.translated_text: "May all spirits and all fears and calamities be pacified for me and all beings, by the name, power, sovereignty, and authority of Great King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>! <s>Svāhā</s>!"

body.text: atha virūpākṣo mahārājo 'bhyudgamyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ kṛtvā bhagavantam eva namasyamāno bhagavantam etad avocat / asmat pariṣado bhadanta bhagavan nāgasuparṇīgrahagṛhītasya īdṛśaṃ rūpalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Then the Great King <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, rising from his seat, draping his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, joining his palms toward the Blessed One, paying homage to the Blessed One, spoke thus to the Blessed One: "Venerable Blessed One, this is the form and characteristics of one seized by a <s>nāga</s>-or-<s>suparṇī</s>-spirit of my assembly:

children.text: hikkate śvasate cāpi śītalaṃ gātram eva ca /
children.translated_text: "He hiccups and pants, and his body becomes cold;

children.text: svidyate phenalālāsya svapate ca punaḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: he sweats, his mouth foams with saliva, and he falls asleep again and again.

children.text: varṇavān bhavate śūro vepate dhāvate tathā /
children.translated_text: He becomes handsome and brave, trembles and runs about,

children.text: punar nakhān vidarśayati mahīṃ viśati roditi //
children.translated_text: then he shows his nails, enters the earth, and weeps."

body.text: tatra mantrapadāny asti lokanātha śṛṇohi me //
body.translated_text: "For this, there are <s>mantra</s>-words—O World-Protector, hear me!"

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: "Let it be thus:"

body.text: kragame / krakamaṇi / krakase / krakaśase / kruśume / krukeke / krukhume krume / agale / nagale / samaṅgale / kuhume / hume / aluke / kalamake / kalale / ire mire / dhire dhire agaruvati svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>kragame / krakamaṇi / krakase / krakaśase / kruśume / krukeke / krukhume krume / agale / nagale / samaṅgale / kuhume / hume / aluke / kalamake / kalale / ire mire / dhire dhire agaruvati svāhā</s>

body.text: svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca virūpākṣasya mahārājasya nāmnā balenaiśvaryādhipatyena ca svāhā //
body.translated_text: "May there be well-being for me and all beings, by the name, power, sovereignty, and authority of Great King <s>Virūpākṣa</s>! <s>Svāhā</s>!"

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tāvad eva sarvāvatyāḥ pariṣadaḥ purataḥ siṃhanādaṃ nadati / daśabalasamanvāgato 'haṃ caturvaiśāradyaviśāradaḥ pariṣady udāram ārṣabhaṃ samyaksiṃhanādaṃ nadāmi / brahmacakraṃ pravartayāmi / māro nirjita ekena sasainyabalavāhanaḥ / rakṣāyai sarvasatvānāṃ sarve vidyāṃ śṛṇātha me //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, before all of this assembly, roared the lion's roar: "I am endowed with the ten powers, skilled in the four kinds of fearlessness. In the assembly I roar the noble, supreme, perfect lion's roar. I set in motion the wheel of <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Māra</s> with his army, forces, and vehicles has been vanquished by one alone. For the protection of all beings, hear all of you my <s>vidyā</s>!"

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: "Let it be thus:"

body.text: asaṅge / khaṅgavate / balavate / balanirghoṣe / śūre śūravate / vajraṃgame / vajradhare / stambhe jambhe / dṛḍhasāre / viraje / vighase / varāgraprāpte / araṇe dharmayukte diśi vighuṣṭe svāhā //
body.translated_text: Unattached! Sword-bearing! Powerful! Resounding with strength! Heroic and valorous! <s>Vajra</s>-bodied! <s>Vajra</s>-bearing! Paralyzer! Crusher! Of firm essence! Stainless! Devourer! Attainer of the highest goal! Sheltering! Righteous! Proclaimed in the directions! <s>Svāhā</s>!

body.text: svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca tathāgatasya nāmnā balenaiśvaryādhipatyena ca svāhā //
body.translated_text: May there be well-being for me and for all beings, by the name, power, sovereignty, and authority of the <s>Tathāgata</s>! <s>Svāhā</s>!

children.translated_text: Having heard the words of the <s>Buddha</s>, the world-protectors of the four directions,
frightened, terrified, and alarmed, stood with palms joined.
The remaining hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), frightened, scattered, and dispersed,
flee in the ten directions, uttering a great cry.
Knowing this, the great kings proclaimed the triple restraint:
'Ah! This <s>vidyā</s> (spell) is a great <s>vidyā</s>, the <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī</s> (Great Crusher of Thousands)!

children.text: yasyāṃ trasanti bhūtāni śrutvā buddhasya bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: At which the <s>bhūtas</s> tremble upon hearing the <s>Buddha</s>'s utterance,
like a blazing fire whose rays are extinguished by the winds.'
'This <s>vidyā</s>, sharp as a razor's edge, has been proclaimed by <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: yo hy etan nābhimanyeta ṛṣivākyaṃ subhāṣitam //
children.translated_text: Whoever does not respect this well-spoken word of the <s>Ṛṣi</s>,
by the curse of <s>Brahmā</s>, his eldest son shall not be spared.
Having kindled a fire and taking black mustard seeds,
mixed with clarified butter, they should be cast into the fire.

children.text: heṣṭham ūrdhvaṃ caturdikṣu kṣiptvā ca varuṇodakam //
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled water of <s>Varuṇa</s> below, above, and in the four directions,

children.text: yadi kṣipraṃ na muñceyuḥ śrutvā buddhasya bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: if they do not quickly release upon hearing the <s>Buddha</s>'s utterance,
may they all be set ablaze like mustard seeds in ghee upon fire!

children.text: kṣemaṃ ca tena lapsyanti yakṣadaṇḍena tarjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: They shall obtain safety, threatened by the rod of the <s>yakṣas</s>.
On their right sides shall arise a great swelling.
They shall become disfigured, afflicted by <s>yakṣa</s>-disease.

children.text: aḍakavatīṃ rājadhānīṃ na gacchanti kadā cana //
children.translated_text: They shall never go to <s>Aḍakavatī</s>, the royal capital.
They shall not see the dwelling of the illustrious <s>Kubera</s>.

children.text: āsanaṃ ca na lapsyanti bhūtasaṃghāḥ samāgame //
children.translated_text: They shall not obtain a seat in the assembly of <s>bhūtas</s>.
They shall be born deprived of food and drink in the <s>yakṣa</s>-circle,
the <s>yakṣa</s> who does not follow the <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardana Sūtra</s>.
<s>Vajradhara</s>, enraged, shall split his head.
With a rough razor's edge he shall cut off his tongue.

children.text: tīkṣṇeṇa cāsya śastreṇa karṇau nāsāṃ ca cchetsyati /
children.translated_text: And with a sharp weapon he shall cut off his ears and nose.
With a razor-edged discus he shall sever his head.
With an iron hammer-spike he shall pierce his heart.

children.text: mukhataḥ sravate cāsya pūyam uṣṇaṃ ca śoṇitam //
children.translated_text: And from his mouth shall flow pus and hot blood.
By the noose and rod of the <s>vidyā</s>, those who forever wander in <s>saṃsāra</s>,
shall continue to wander there in the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>.'
The great kings, endowed with glory, having assembled from the four directions,
clad in the armor of <s>Dharma</s>, sat upon auspicious seats.
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> in the east, <s>Virūḍhaka</s> in the south,
<s>Virūpākṣa</s> in the west, and <s>Kubera</s> in the northern direction.

children.text: rājñāṃ samāgatānāṃ hi jvalatāṃ tejasā śriyā /
children.translated_text: When the kings had assembled, blazing with splendor and glory,

children.text: antarīkṣaṃ tadā śāśtā sarvajño hi samudgataḥ //
children.translated_text: the Teacher, the Omniscient One, then rose into the sky.
Seated upon the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond throne) in a palace fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s>,
then <s>Brahmā</s>, the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, stands with palms joined in reverence.
Like a golden mountain, resplendent, resembling molten gold,
blossoming like a lotus flower, like a king of <s>śāla</s> trees in bloom,
like the full moon or the sun surrounded by stars,
the Sage, of golden-hued body, was adorned with the marks.
Having praised the Illuminator of the World, <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandfather of the World,
spoke to the World-Protectors in the presence of the Lord of the World:
'The assembly of the World-Protectors has not received instruction.

children.text: ito buddhā hi jāyante buddhāḥ pratyekajā api //
children.translated_text: From here are <s>Buddhas</s> born, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> as well.

children.text: itaś ca śrāvakotpattir devāś cāpi samutsthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: From here arise <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), and gods also have arisen.
From here are born <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, masters of the six limbs of the <s>Vedas</s>.
<s>Ṛṣis</s> of great fortune, from here come <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Through your negligence, the human race is being destroyed.'
Having heard <s>Brahmā</s>'s words, the World-Protectors spoke:

children.text: evam etan mahābrahmann evam etat mahāmune //
children.translated_text: 'So it is, O Great <s>Brahmā</s>, so it is, O Great Sage!
We shall purify the ocean on all sides.

children.text: sumeruṃ kaṃpayitvā tu dhāraṇīṃ parivartya ca //
children.translated_text: Having shaken <s>Sumeru</s> and having turned the earth,
we shall bind with a noose the moon, sun, and wind,
and all the stars, with a tight grip.

children.text: diśaś cādarśanā bhāgās teṣāṃ neṣyāma sarvadā /
children.translated_text: The invisible regions of the directions we shall always lead away

children.text: ye praduṣṭā bhaviṣyanti na ca lokahitodyataḥ //
children.translated_text: those who become corrupted and are not devoted to the welfare of the world.

children.text: lokaḥ sadevako hy eṣa garhate bhūtakāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: For this world with its gods reproaches the cause of evil spirits.
Spirits overcome and harm the human race.
Here the mantra-holders freely display their prowess.

children.text: atikrāmanti ye vidyāṃ mantrān auṣadham eva vā //
children.translated_text: Those who transgress the <s>vidyā</s>, the mantras, or the medicines,
the assemblies that have transgressed the <s>vidyā</s>, threatened with punishment on all sides,
we shall seize and bring them before the Lord of the World.

children.text: teṣāṃ daṇḍaṃ praṇeṣyāmaḥ sūtraṃ brahmaṇā nirmitam /
children.translated_text: We shall impose upon them the punishment of the <s>sūtra</s> fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s>.
When this is spoken, the entire host of <s>bhūtas</s> in the universe trembles.'

children.text: buddhasya pādau vanditvā ālokya ca parasparam /
children.translated_text: Having saluted the feet of the <s>Buddha</s> and looking at one another,
[they prepared chariots] of gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), pearl, and crystal,
and of <s>musārāgalva</s> (cat's-eye gem), filled with the seven treasures,
four chariots with a thousand spokes, golden, well-fashioned,
yoked by <s>Viśvakarman</s>, moving through the sky by supernatural power.
Mounting those chariots, the kings set forth to the host of <s>bhūtas</s>.

children.text: puṣpapūrṇāṃ mahīṃ kṛtvā cūrṇaiś cāpi hiraṇmayaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having covered the earth with flowers and with golden powders,

children.text: yaṣṭīr ābadhya hi gale sūtrapāśāṃs tathāpi ca //
children.translated_text: and having bound staffs around their necks and nooses of <s>sūtra</s> (thread) as well,
having dispatched all the <s>yakṣa</s>-generals in the four directions:
'Bring all beings, as many as are in the directions under our sway,

children.text: sāhasrapramardanaṃ hy etet saṃśrautuṃ sūtram uttamam /
children.translated_text: to hear this supreme <s>sūtra</s>, the <s>Sāhasrapramardana</s>,
arisen from the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, contemplated by all worlds.'
The <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> were subdued by the great thousandfold body.
Having heard the words of <s>Kubera</s>, the <s>yakṣa</s>-general departed.
The <s>guhyakas</s> (secret beings), striding in the four directions, proclaimed the proclamation.

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśac ca bhūtāni grahā gandharvajā mune //
children.translated_text: Twenty-eight <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>grahas</s> (seizers) born of <s>gandharvas</s>, O Sage!
'In this eastern quarter, let the hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> hear me!
All of you are afflicted by the five bonds of the <s>sūtra</s>-noose.

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśac ca bhūtāni grahāḥ kumbhāṇḍajā mune /
children.translated_text: Twenty-eight <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>grahas</s> born of <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, O Sage!
In this southern quarter, let the hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> hear me!
All of you are afflicted by the five bonds of the <s>sūtra</s>-noose.

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśac ca bhūtāni bhonti nāgagrahā mune /
children.translated_text: Twenty-eight <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>grahas</s> of <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), O Sage!
In this western quarter, let the hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> hear me!

body.text: sarve te sūtrapāśena pañcabandhanapīḍitāḥ /
body.translated_text: All of you are afflicted by the five bonds of the <s>sūtra</s>-noose.

children.text: aṣṭāviṃśac ca bhūtāni bhonti yakṣagrahā mune /
children.translated_text: Twenty-eight <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>grahas</s> of <s>yakṣas</s>, O Sage!

children.text: digbhāge uttare cāpi bhūtasaṃghāḥ śṛṇontu me //
children.translated_text: In the northern quarter as well, let the hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> hear me!
All of you are afflicted by the five bonds of the <s>sūtra</s>-noose.
The eldest son of <s>Kubera</s> is <s>Sañjaya</s>, whose vehicle is men.
At his very feet are sixty <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>yakṣas</s>,
drawn by the <s>sūtra</s>-noose, afflicted by the five bonds.

children.text: putro dvitīyas tasyaiva janako nāma viśrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: His second son is the renowned one named <s>Janaka</s>.
At his very feet are sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yakṣas</s>,
drawn by the <s>sūtra</s>-noose, afflicted by the five bonds.

children.text: putras tritīyas tasyaiva nāmnā cāsau mahāgrahaḥ //
children.translated_text: His third son is the one named <s>Mahāgraha</s> (the Great Seizer).
At his very feet are sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yakṣas</s>,
drawn by the <s>sūtra</s>-noose, afflicted by the five bonds.
His fourth son is the one named <s>Kalaśodara</s> (Pot-Belly).
At his very feet are sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yakṣas</s>,
drawn by the <s>sūtra</s>-noose, afflicted by the five bonds.
<s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, four-armed, of great strength,
at his very feet are sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yakṣas</s>,
drawn by the <s>sūtra</s>-noose, afflicted by the five bonds.
All the <s>bhūtas</s> having come to the mountain of <s>Bhūtamardana</s> (Spirit-Crusher),
this <s>vidyā</s> was proclaimed, the all-<s>vidyā</s> that brings peace.

children.text: niṣṭhuraṃ puruṣaṃ daṇḍaṃ sarvabuddhair hi bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: The harsh human punishment has been spoken by all the <s>Buddhas</s>.

children.text: eṣa gacchāmaḥ śaraṇaṃ sarve gautamam ādarāt //
children.translated_text: 'Let us all go with reverence to <s>Gautama</s> for refuge.
Follow him without deceit, and do not fear in any way.'
Then in a mere moment, the hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> assembled.
Those stationed in mountains, precipices, oceans, and lakes,
in rivers, springs, waterfalls, and whirlpools,
in gardens, palaces, pleasure-groves, and forests,
in sacred sites, villages, and at the roots of trees,
at the entrances of cities, in towns and settlements,

children.text: rājakuleṣu dvāreṣu vimāneṣu ca ye sthitāḥ //
children.translated_text: in royal courts, at gateways, and in palaces,
in pavilions, cremation grounds, and in temples,
at boundaries, toll-houses, empty dwellings, and in wilderness,

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ heṣṭhaṃ ca ye yakṣāś caturdikṣu vidikṣu ca /
children.translated_text: whatever <s>yakṣas</s> above, below, in the four directions and intermediate directions,
thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>yakṣas</s> were drawn by the <s>vidyā</s>-noose.
Some played <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> (drums), some played <s>gargara</s> (a type of drum),
and the mighty ones played <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), <s>paṇavas</s> (small drums), and flutes.

children.text: kṛtvā ca vāditaṃ citraṃ gāndharvaṃ nāṭyam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Having made wonderful music and <s>gāndharva</s> (celestial) dance as well,

children.text: indraḥ somaś ca varuṇo bharadvājaḥ prajāpatiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>,
<s>Mātali</s>, <s>Lohitākṣa</s>, <s>Himavanta</s>, <s>Supūrṇaka</s>,
<s>Candana</s>, <s>Kāmaśreṣṭhī</s>, <s>Maṇikaṇṭha</s>, <s>Nikaṇṭhaka</s>,

children.text: prajāgurur yatīśaś ca devasūtaś ca mātaliḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāguru</s>, <s>Yatīśa</s>, <s>Devasūta</s>, and <s>Mātali</s>,
<s>Citrasena</s> the <s>gandharva</s>, <s>Nararāja</s>, <s>Jinarṣabha</s>,
likewise the one named <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, <s>Tumburu</s>, <s>Sūryavarcas</s>,
<s>Śaila</s>, <s>Asiputra</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Yaśodhara</s>,
<s>Āḍavaka</s>, <s>Sumanas</s>, <s>Śūcīkarṇa</s>, <s>Darīmukha</s>,
<s>Pañcālagaṇḍa</s>, <s>Sumukha</s>, with their armies and forces and vehicles.

children.text: devā nāgāś ca gandharvā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: traitīyakaś ca unmādās tathā cāturthako jvarāḥ //
children.translated_text: and tertian fevers, madnesses, and quartan fevers,

children.text: ye ca lokaṃ viheṭhanti praduṣṭā yakṣarākṣasāḥ /
children.translated_text: and the corrupted <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s> who torment the world,
having been brought from the four directions, afflicted by the five bonds,
standing before him with palms joined, they spoke to the Lord of the World:

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottama //
children.translated_text: 'Homage to you, O Hero among Men! Homage to you, O Supreme Person!
With palms joined we bow—O King of <s>Dharma</s>, homage to you!'

children.text: dhāvanti puratas teṣāṃ bhūtā yakṣā mahābhayāḥ //
children.translated_text: Running before them are terrifying <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>yakṣas</s>,
four-armed, greatly terrible, many-footed and one-footed,
four-footed and two-footed, with feet upward and faces downward,
many-bodied with one head, and one-bodied with four heads,
many-eyed, great-bodied, one-eyed, twelve-bellied,
with donkey-lips and elephant-heads, with hands upward and heads downward,
<s>rākṣasas</s> with weapon-teeth, weapon-arms, and weapon-feet,
copper-haired, copper-handed, copper-eyed, copper-palmed,
with copper hammer-feet, copper-nosed, and iron-faced,
with blazing hands and feet, yet standing in human form,

children.text: kāṇāḥ kubjās tu garuḍā vikṛtākṣā vijṛmbhakāḥ //
children.translated_text: one-eyed, hunchbacked, eagle-like, with distorted eyes and yawning mouths,
with forms of <s>makaras</s> (sea-monsters) and <s>vyāḍas</s> (mythical beasts), deformed, with all faces turned upward,
with hanging lips and crooked teeth, malicious, with frowning faces,
pot-bellied, jar-eared, pendulous-eared, and earless,
long-eared, long-armed, with long hair-tips in their hands,
withered-bodied, long-bodied, long-haired, well-adorned,
heavy-footed, thin-necked, foul-smelling, with hands for bellies,
with limbs like those of a <s>makara</s>, with pestle-hammer bellies,
with upturned eyes, great-eared, with upstanding hair, very red,
thick-headed, bow-necked, hunchbacked pot-bellied, and emaciated—
they rained fire-showers, having roamed the peak of <s>Meru</s>,
the foremost summit of trees, mountains, and boulders, equal in splendor.
<s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s> with voices like conches, <s>bherīs</s> (kettledrums), <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, and <s>dundubhis</s> (war-drums),
release terrible roars, great-throated, with harsh voices,
black, blue, brown, green, tawny, and yellow,
<s>guhyakas</s> (secret beings), standing before the abodes of all the wicked,
devouring the human world—men, women, and others.
Some devour flesh, blood, fat, and marrow of the slain,
with needle-hair and sword-hair, smeared with red blood,
eating as they run about, seizing corpses indeed,
sharp-toothed, red-handed, their lips smeared with blood,
with hands filled with half-eaten limbs,
devouring kidneys, hearts, collarbones, and hips,
the terrifying ones steal strength from living beings through their hands and feet,
with bodies made of heaped bones, they frighten multitudes of people.
Seizing human skin filled with blood,
mixed with fierce poison, they hurl it in the ten directions.
At the entrances of cities they throw confusion upon families.

children.text: vātaṃ pittaṃ ca śleṣmāṇaṃ kṣobhayanti caturdiśam //
children.translated_text: They disturb wind, bile, and phlegm in the four directions.
Thus they stand there, those terrifying afflicters of kings.
All of them too, having assembled, are drawn by the <s>vidyā</s>-noose.
'Homage to you, O Hero among Men! Homage to you, O Supreme Person!
With palms joined we bow—O King of <s>Dharma</s>, homage to you!'
They roam through cities, villages, kingdoms, and royal courts,
the terrifying <s>yakṣas</s>, stealers of vital energy, feeders on human flesh and blood.
Of great bodies, greatly terrifying, of great strength, great lords,
ten-headed, thousand-eyed, of great appetite, great-mouthed,
with a great retinue, weapons in hand, most fearsome,
grasping serpent-skin shields, holding torches, four-armed,
staff-handed, weapon-handed, trident-bearers, <s>vajra</s>-wielders,
they terrify all the directions, raising a most dreadful battle-cry.

children.text: prasannā guhyakāḥ sarve duṣṭānām ālaye sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All the <s>Guhyakas</s> (secret ones), well-disposed, stationed at the abodes of the wicked,
devour men and women in the human world, and others likewise.

children.text: uṣṇair māṃsaiś ca rudhirair bhāntāṅgāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Their limbs shining with warm flesh and blood, shape-shifters,
taking the forms of lions, tigers, she-buffaloes, cows, donkeys, camels, and elephants,
in the forms of bears, leopards, wolves, <s>nyaṅku</s> deer, jackals, rams, and cats,
in forms resembling mice and monkeys, rhinoceroses, boars, and mongooses,
in the forms of fish and turtles, and also of crows and cuckoos,
owls, vultures, hawks, and also great fish and sea-monsters,
in the forms of peacocks, geese, pigeons, herons, and other birds—
some <s>Yakṣas</s> watch humans in the form of roosters.
In the guise of <s>Suparṇī</s> birds they terrify many people.
Some have human heads and bodies like donkeys, hideous;
others are seen rushing at other beings, with deranged minds,
naked, devoted to desire, wrapped in garlands of entrails.
They strike with tridents, they cause torment to living beings,

children.text: muñcanti dāruṇaṃ śvāsaṃ saṃtāpenti imāḥ prajāḥ //
children.translated_text: they release terrible breath, they afflict these creatures.
They are seen in various forms, as many as there are classes of living beings;
some hold mountains, others bear swords and <s>cakras</s> (discuses).
Hundreds of thousands in number, threatening with pestles and clubs,
<s>Rākṣasas</s> with eyes gouged out, faces averted, with broken teeth,
with severed noses, severed ears, severed tongues, wrinkled faces,
and <s>Rākṣasas</s> with hands and feet cut off, and heads severed.

children.text: prekṣanti cāvatāraṃ hi ojo hiṃsanti kilbiṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: They watch for openings and, being sinful, harm the vital force;
in the bodies of humans, a very subtle spirit-seizure is observed.
In the spaces between hairs, at vital points, and at the mouths of wounds—
all of them have assembled, drawn by the noose of the <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge).

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottama /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O hero among men! Homage to you, O Supreme Person!
We salute you with joined palms; to <s>Dharmarāja</s>, homage to you!

children.text: sumerau girirāje ca cakravāḍe tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: On <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, and on <s>Cakravāḍa</s> likewise,
on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>, <s>Īśādhāra</s>, <s>Himavat</s>, and <s>Gandhamādana</s>,
on <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, and on the twin mountains of <s>Nārada</s>,

children.text: śrīparvatasya mūrdhasthāḥ śṛṅgā ye bhṛśam udgatāḥ //
children.translated_text: on the summit of <s>Śrīparvata</s>, the peaks that rise exceedingly high—

children.text: yās tatra devatādhastā ṛṣayaś ca tathādhikāḥ /
children.translated_text: whatever deities and sages, and those still greater, dwell there—
even they became agitated, their lifespans shortened, their minds alarmed.
Thousands of <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of gods, and hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of gods,
divine maidens of great fortune, having joined their palms indeed,

children.text: vemacitrī rāhulaś ca prahlādaś ca samāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vemacitri</s>, <s>Rāhula</s>, and <s>Prahlāda</s> assembled,
with thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of servants and hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of servants.
Their daughters, possessed of supernatural powers, joined their palms with ten nails.

children.text: sāgaraḥ supratiṣṭhaś ca nāgarājo manasvy api //
children.translated_text: <s>Sāgara</s> and <s>Supratiṣṭha</s>, the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Manasvin</s>,
<s>Nagendra</s>, <s>Anavatapta</s>, and both <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Upanandaka</s>,

children.text: vakṣunando vajramatir gaṅgā sindhuś ca sāgaraḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Vakṣunanda</s>, <s>Vajramati</s>, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, and <s>Sāgara</s>,
<s>Suparṇī</s> and the bird-kings who churn the ocean,
with thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Nāgas</s> and hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Nāgas</s>—

children.text: kanyās teṣāṃ mahābhāgā añjaliṃ saṃpragṛhya vai /
children.translated_text: their daughters of great fortune, having joined their palms indeed,
and both <s>Ravi</s> (Sun) and <s>Candra</s> (Moon), attended by the constellations,
<s>Suvarṇavarṇa</s> among the <s>Puṣpa</s> people, <s>Rabheyaka</s> in <s>Magadha</s>,
<s>Kāpili</s> in <s>Bharukaccha</s>, <s>Prapuṇḍaka</s> in <s>Kośala</s>,

children.text: śūcīlomā ca madreṣu malleṣu ca yaśodharaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śūcīlomā</s> in <s>Madra</s>, and <s>Yaśodhara</s> in <s>Malla</s>,

children.text: vibhīṣaṇaś ca pāñcāle lohitākṣaś ca aśvaje //
children.translated_text: <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> in <s>Pāñcāla</s>, and <s>Lohitākṣa</s> in <s>Aśvaka</s>,

children.text: piṅgalaś ca avanteṣu kapilākṣaś ca vaidiśe /
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgala</s> in <s>Avanti</s>, and <s>Kapilākṣa</s> in <s>Vaidiśa</s>,

children.text: kumbhodaraś ca matseṣu sūrateṣu ca dīrghilaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhodara</s> in <s>Matsya</s>, and <s>Dīrghila</s> in <s>Sūrata</s>,

children.text: pramardanas tu gāndhāre sūryamitraś ca kambuṣu /
children.translated_text: <s>Pramardana</s> in <s>Gāndhāra</s>, and <s>Sūryamitra</s> in <s>Kambu</s>—
these fourteen <s>Yakṣas</s> have been declared in the great regions.
<s>Vajrapāṇi</s> the great <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Dharmapāla</s>, <s>Prapuṇḍara</s>,
<s>Kapila</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Piṇḍāra</s>, <s>Karaśodara</s>,

children.text: kumbhīraḥ sātyakiś cāpi pāñcikaś ca jinarṣabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbhīra</s>, <s>Sātyaki</s>, <s>Pāñcika</s>, and <s>Jinarṣabha</s>,
<s>Maheśvara</s>, the great <s>Yakṣa</s>, four-armed, of great strength,
<s>Pramardana</s>, <s>Śūrasena</s>, <s>Mahānagna</s>, of great power,

children.text: yamaś ca yamadūtaś ca māraś cāpi sasainyakaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s>, <s>Yamadūta</s>, and <s>Māra</s> with his army,

children.text: harir nāmnā tv asau yakṣo yakṣakoṭīparigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: a <s>Yakṣa</s> named <s>Hari</s>, surrounded by <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Yakṣas</s>,

children.text: hārītī ca sasainyā tu giridāri ca yakṣiṇī //
children.translated_text: and <s>Hārītī</s> with her army, and the <s>Yakṣiṇī</s> <s>Giridāri</s>,
of terrifying form, of great splendor, the renowned <s>Hārītī</s>,
<s>Caṇḍā</s> and <s>Caṇḍālikā</s>, surrounded by five hundred sons,
<s>Ākoṭā</s>, <s>Karkaṭī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Padumā</s>, <s>Padumāvatī</s>,

children.text: puṣpadantī viśālā ca kharakarṇā ca rākṣasī //
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣpadantī</s>, <s>Viśālā</s>, and the <s>Rākṣasī</s> <s>Kharakarṇā</s>,
<s>Candana</s>, <s>Viṣṇula</s>, <s>Haripiṅgala</s>, and <s>Piṅgala</s>,
<s>Kuñjara</s>, <s>Nāgadanta</s>, <s>Girimitra</s>, and <s>Agradaṃṣṭraka</s>,

children.text: rākṣasī bhadradantā ca brahmilā viṣṇulā tathā /
children.translated_text: the <s>Rākṣasī</s> <s>Bhadradantā</s>, <s>Brahmilā</s>, and <s>Viṣṇulā</s>,

children.text: yakṣo hālāhalaś caiva rākṣasaś ca vituṇḍakaḥ //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Yakṣa</s> <s>Hālāhala</s>, and the <s>Rākṣasa</s> <s>Vituṇḍaka</s>.

children.text: śūleṣu te gṛhītvātha gavāś ca mṛgamānuṣān /
children.translated_text: Seizing on tridents cattle, deer, and humans,

children.text: bhakṣayantaś ca jīvanto dhāvantaś ca diśodiśaḥ //
children.translated_text: they devour living beings and race in every direction.
They make the earth tremble, they wither the forest-trees,
they crush the mountain peaks and oppress these creatures.
Inciting one another, drawn by the <s>vidyā</s>, they have assembled;
of all those assembled, and in the presence of the Lord of the World,
then <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> the king addressed the Lord of the World:
"In the northern quarter I have a well-built royal capital,
the delightful <s>Aḍakavatī</s>; hence I am the lord of <s>Aḍaka</s>.
It was conceived by all the gods, the royal capital called <s>Aḍaka</s>.
Its ramparts rise high, filled with the seven treasures,
fashioned of golden materials in two rows at each <s>yojana</s>.
At each single row, on all four sides,
<s>Yakṣas</s> stand bearing <s>vajras</s>, weapons in hand, well-armored.
That very royal capital has four gates:
one gate is made of gold, the second wrought of silver,
the third gate of crystal, the fourth inlaid with gems.

children.text: asty antare tu nagare udyāne vanapuṣpite //
children.translated_text: Within the city there are gardens with flowering groves,
wonderful aerial palaces made of the seven treasures,
trees of various gems, resounding with the songs of various birds,
covered with various flowers, anointed with various fragrances,
adorned with the sports of birds and with songs and instruments.

children.text: anubhomi śriyaṃ tv agryāṃ bhūtānāṃ tatra maṇḍale /
children.translated_text: I enjoy supreme splendor among beings in that <s>maṇḍala</s>;
endowed with all excellent qualities, there are my attendants.
They follow <s>dharma</s>, love <s>dharma</s>, and do not harm living beings.

children.text: annapānais tu vikalā dāruṇās tv itarāḥ prajāḥ //
children.translated_text: But other creatures, deprived of food and drink, are terrible.
They follow <s>adharma</s>, love <s>adharma</s>, and harm living beings.
Seeking wealth, they gaze in the four directions.
Those stationed at city gates, in gardens, and in forests—
the hosts of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Bhūtas</s>—
I shall bring them all, drawn by the noose of the <s>sūtra</s>.
Shaded by groves of sandalwood, dotted with cool lotus-ponds,
in the midst of that royal capital is the dwelling of <s>Dharmarāja</s>.

children.text: samantād yojanaṃ yāvat kūṭāgārās tu nirmitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All around, extending for a <s>yojana</s>, mansions are built:

children.text: suvarnasya bhaved eko dvitīyo rūpyam eva ca /
children.translated_text: one would be of gold, the second of silver,

children.text: vaiḍūryasya tṛtīyas tu caturthaḥ sphāṭikaḥ śuciḥ //
children.translated_text: the third of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), the fourth of pure crystal,
the fifth of red pearls, the sixth of <s>aśmagarbha</s> (emerald),
the seventh of <s>musāra</s> (coral), and the eighth made of all seven treasures.
Hundreds of thousands of women assemble in each one,

children.text: citrair ābharaṇair agraiś citrair veśair alaṃkṛtāḥ //
children.translated_text: adorned with the finest and most wonderful ornaments and garments,
trained in various songs, instruments, and arts.
With such delight, exalted, with a contented mind,
there I, intoxicated with mead and desires, am greatly exalted.
My assembly flees, terrified in all ten directions,

children.text: striyaś ca puruṣāś caiva tathā dārakadārikāḥ /
children.translated_text: women and men alike, and also boys and girls.
Even those in the womb perish, and those born in animal wombs.
The constellations, moon, and sun—the planets afflict terribly.

children.text: sasyaṃ bījaṃ phalaṃ puṣpam oṣadhaṃ pānabhojanam //
children.translated_text: Grain, seed, fruit, flower, herbs, drink, and food—

children.text: harante mānuṣīṃ lakṣmīm uccānīcīṃ karonti ca /
children.translated_text: they steal human prosperity and cause ups and downs.

children.text: ye kecid duṣkṛtā loke vairāḥ kalahavigrahāḥ //
children.translated_text: Whatever evil deeds exist in the world—enmities, quarrels, conflicts—

children.text: dagdhaṃ naṣṭaṃ hataṃ bhinnaṃ tat sarvaṃ bhūtajaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: what is burned, lost, slain, or broken—all that is said to be caused by <s>Bhūtas</s>.
They veil, they uncover, they overturn, they stand fast,

children.text: uttrāsenti ca satvānāṃ viprekṣanti dviṣanti ca /
children.translated_text: they terrify beings, they gaze with hostility,

children.text: darśenti pāpakān svapnān prasuptān pīḍayanti ca //
children.translated_text: they show evil dreams and torment those who are asleep.

children.text: dvārasthāś cācchaṭāṃ kṛtvā prakrośanti grasanti ca /
children.translated_text: Standing at doors, they snap their fingers, they shriek, they devour.
They are seen in the forms of friends and kinsmen, and they speak.
In the forms of beautiful maidens they are seen, being shape-shifters;
they are seen in the form of the moon, taking the forms of sun and stars.
In the form of wind, meteors, and lightning they are seen, those who afflict with wind;
resembling clusters of meteors, with jackal-voices, terrifying.
They are seen striding about in trees, <s>caityas</s> (shrines), and temples;
in the form of boys, blazing, with cart-like voices.

children.text: sadā citrāṇi darśenti ālayeṣu patheṣu ca /
children.translated_text: They constantly show strange things in dwellings and on roads;

children.text: gṛhāṇāṃ nagarāṇāṃ ca dvāre muñcanti te grahāḥ /
children.translated_text: at the gates of houses and cities they release these spirit-seizures.

children.text: gṛhītvā jīvitaṃ kāyaṃ kupathe grāmayanti ca /
children.translated_text: Having seized the life-force and the body, they lead one astray on evil paths.

children.text: vicitrāṇi ca rūpāṇi vicitrāṇi svarāṇi ca //
children.translated_text: Various are their forms, and various are their voices;

children.text: rogān vicitrān darśenti vyādhīn vai kāyasaṃsthitān /
children.translated_text: they display various diseases and ailments situated in the body;

children.text: viparītaṃ ca darśenti sarvarogeṣu ca lakṣaṇam //
children.translated_text: they show perverted signs in all diseases.

children.text: yāvatī prakṛti loke sarvān darśenti te 'nyathā /
children.translated_text: Whatever natural order exists in the world, they show it all otherwise.
All of them have assembled, drawn by the noose of the <s>vidyā</s>.

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottama /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O hero among men! Homage to you, O Supreme Person!
We salute you with joined palms; to <s>Dharmarāja</s>, homage to you!
Then King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> rose and, with palms joined,
shining like gold, with wheel-marked and beautifully adorned feet,
O great sage whose radiance illuminates the world, equal to fire!
Sixty-four thousand <s>Yakṣas</s> here are terrible;
they dwell in the northern quarter and afflict those born there.
I shall bring their punishment before the Lord of the World.

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: Let it be thus:

body.text: khaṅge / khaṅgagarbhe / vicakṣaṇe / cakragagane / candre capale / bhīmaparvate / kharāgre / kuṭilakarāgre / ekākṣivargavati / sāraṅgavati vicitrakānti svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca uttarasyāṃ diśi svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>khaṅge</s> / <s>khaṅgagarbhe</s> / <s>vicakṣaṇe</s> / <s>cakragagane</s> / <s>candre capale</s> / <s>bhīmaparvate</s> / <s>kharāgre</s> / <s>kuṭilakarāgre</s> / <s>ekākṣivargavati</s> / <s>sāraṅgavati vicitrakānti</s> — may there be well-being for me and for all beings in the northern direction! <s>Svāhā</s>!

children.text: brahmā cāpy atha śakraś ca lokapālā maheśvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and also <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), the World-Protectors, the Great Lords,
all the generals of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Hārītī</s> with her daughters—

children.text: idaṃ puṣpaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca pratigṛhṇantu mamāhutiṃ /
children.translated_text: may they accept this flower, this fragrance, and my oblation.

children.text: vīryeṇa tejasā teṣām aiśvaryeṇa balena ca //
children.translated_text: By their valor, their splendor, their sovereignty, and their strength,

body.text: nihatāḥ sarvarogāś ca svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvabhayopadravebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: may all diseases be destroyed! May there be well-being for me and for all beings, from all fears and calamities! <s>Svāhā</s>!

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottama /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O hero among men! Homage to you, O Supreme Person!
We salute you with joined palms; to <s>Dharmarāja</s>, homage to you!

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca rājo 'pi sa kṛtāñjalir utthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And King <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> too rose with palms joined,
like a full cluster of blossoms, with a voice like the song of a <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird,
with the thundering sound of peacocks, cuckoos, clouds, and war-drums.
Sixty-four thousand <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, O sage,

body.text: niśritā pūrvadigbhāgaṃ pīḍayanti tadudbhavān /
body.translated_text: dwell in the eastern quarter and afflict those born there.

body.text: teṣāṃ daṇḍaṃ praṇeṣyāmi lokanāthasya saṃmukham //
body.translated_text: I shall bring their punishment before the Lord of the World.

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: Let it be thus:

body.text: dharaṇi dhāraṇi / pradhvaṃsani / bhañjani / prabhañjani / vidhamaṇi / kiṃpuruṣe / sakale / sārathe / sāravati / śūradhare / śūradhāriṇi / śuddhacaraṇe / ghoṣavati / sarāgre / śānti svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca pūrvasyāṃ diśi svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>dharaṇi dhāraṇi</s> / <s>pradhvaṃsani</s> / <s>bhañjani</s> / <s>prabhañjani</s> / <s>vidhamaṇi</s> / <s>kiṃpuruṣe</s> / <s>sakale</s> / <s>sārathe</s> / <s>sāravati</s> / <s>śūradhare</s> / <s>śūradhāriṇi</s> / <s>śuddhacaraṇe</s> / <s>ghoṣavati</s> / <s>sarāgre</s> / <s>śānti</s> — may there be well-being for me and for all beings in the eastern direction! <s>Svāhā</s>!

children.text: brahmā cāpy atha śakraś ca lokapālā maheśvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and also <s>Śakra</s>, the World-Protectors, the Great Lords,
all the generals of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Hārītī</s> with her daughters—

children.text: idaṃ puṣpaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca pratigṛhṇantu mamāhutiṃ /
children.translated_text: may they accept this flower, this fragrance, and my oblation.

children.text: vīryeṇa tejasā teṣām aiśvaryeṇa balena ca //
children.translated_text: By their valor, their splendor, their sovereignty, and their strength,

body.text: nihatāḥ sarvarogāś ca svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvabhayopadravebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: may all diseases be destroyed! May there be well-being for me and for all beings, from all fears and calamities! <s>Svāhā</s>!

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottama /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O hero among men! Homage to you, O Supreme Person!
We salute you with joined palms; to <s>Dharmarāja</s>, homage to you!

children.text: rājā virūḍhakaś cāpi prāñjalīkas tato utthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And King <s>Virūḍhaka</s> too rose with palms joined.
The Omniscient, the All-Seeing, the All-Proclaiming, the Crusher,
the Dispeller of all doubts, the Guide of all worlds—
sixty-four thousand <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Pretas</s>, and <s>Pūtanās</s>
dwell in the southern region and afflict those born there.
I shall bring their punishment before the Lord of the World.

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: Let it be thus:

body.text: śānti śāravati / kānti kāravati / kiṃkarasi / kiraṇḍi / kiṃvaḍi / dharaṇi / vardhani / bhūmidhāriṇi / vibhūmidhāriṇi / himavati / jyotiścaraṇe / mālāgri / svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Śānti</s>, <s>Śāravatī</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Kāravatī</s>, <s>Kiṃkarasi</s>, <s>Kiraṇḍi</s>, <s>Kiṃvaḍi</s>, <s>Dharaṇi</s>, <s>Vardhani</s>, <s>Bhūmidhāriṇī</s>, <s>Vibhūmidhāriṇī</s>, <s>Himavatī</s>, <s>Jyotiścaraṇe</s>, <s>Mālāgri</s>—may there be well-being for me and all sentient beings in the southern direction, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: brahmā cāpy atha śakraś ca lokapālā maheśvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), the world-protectors, the great lords,
all the chiefs of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Hārītī</s> with her children—

children.text: idaṃ puṣpaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca pratigṛhṇantu mamāhutiṃ /
children.translated_text: may they accept this flower and this incense, my oblation;

children.text: vīryeṇa tejasā teṣām aiśvaryeṇa balena ca //
children.translated_text: by their vigor, splendor, sovereignty, and strength,

body.text: nihatāḥ sarvarogāś ca svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca
body.translated_text: may all diseases be destroyed! May there be well-being for me and all sentient beings

body.text: sarvabhayopadravopasargebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: from all fears, calamities, and afflictions, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottama /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O hero among men; homage to you, O supreme among men;
we salute you with palms joined—O <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of Dharma), homage to you!

body.text:
virūpākṣo mahārājā gṛhītāñjalir utthitaḥ /
mahāmeghamahāsiṃhaḥ mahāmahamahodadhiḥ /

children.translated_text: the great proclaimer, the great hero, the crusher of great battles;
sixty-four thousand <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Suparṇas</s> (Garuḍas), and <s>Guhyakas</s>,
having resorted to the western region, they afflict those born there;
I shall impose punishment upon them before the Lord of the World.

body.translated_text: <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the great king, has risen with palms joined: the great cloud, the great lion, the great mass, the great ocean,

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: Let it be thus:

body.text: dharmadharāgre / balavati / balini viśāṅge / vivasi sāgare / khari kapile / caṇḍāli / tiriṇi / virājane / vidhāriṇi / varṇavati / acare / svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca paścimāyāṃ diśi svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Dharmadharāgre</s>, <s>Balavatī</s>, <s>Balinī</s>, <s>Viśāṅge</s>, <s>Vivasī</s>, <s>Sāgare</s>, <s>Khari</s>, <s>Kapile</s>, <s>Caṇḍālī</s>, <s>Tiriṇī</s>, <s>Virājane</s>, <s>Vidhāriṇī</s>, <s>Varṇavatī</s>, <s>Acare</s>—may there be well-being for me and all sentient beings in the western direction, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: brahmā cāpy atha śakraś ca lokapālā maheśvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, the world-protectors, the great lords,
all the chiefs of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Hārītī</s> with her children—

children.text: idaṃ puṣpaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca pratigṛhṇantu mamāhutiṃ /
children.translated_text: may they accept this flower and this incense, my oblation;

children.text: vīryeṇa tejasā teṣām aiśvaryeṇa balena ca //
children.translated_text: by their vigor, splendor, sovereignty, and strength,

body.text: nihatāḥ sarvarogāś ca svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvabhayopadravopasargebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: may all diseases be destroyed! May there be well-being for me and all sentient beings from all fears, calamities, and afflictions, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottama /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O hero among men; homage to you, O supreme among men;
we salute you with palms joined—O <s>Dharmarāja</s>, homage to you!

body.text:
atha brahmā mahābrahmā prāñjalīkaḥ samutthitaḥ /
brāhmaṇaḥ snātakaḥ śuddhaḥ sarvavedeṣu pāragaḥ /

children.translated_text: the king of physicians, the delight of people, the healer of all diseases;
whatever <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s> are stationed in the directions and intermediate directions,

children.text: pātāle heṣṭham ūrdhvaṃ ca ākāśe niśritā grahāḥ /
children.translated_text: in the netherworld, below, above, and the planets stationed in the sky—
I shall impose punishment upon them before the Lord of the World.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, the great <s>Brahmā</s>, has risen with palms joined: the Brahmin, the graduate, the pure one, who has crossed to the far shore of all the <s>Vedas</s>,

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: Let it be thus:

body.text: brahma brahmaghoṣe / brahmasvare / vajradhare / sthire / sāre / acale / araṇe / iṣaṇe / araṇi deraṇi / śūre / varāgraprāpte / sāravate /
body.translated_text: <s>Brahma</s>, <s>Brahmaghoṣe</s>, <s>Brahmasvare</s>, <s>Vajradhare</s>, <s>Sthire</s>, <s>Sāre</s>, <s>Acale</s>, <s>Araṇe</s>, <s>Iṣaṇe</s>, <s>Araṇi</s>, <s>Deraṇi</s>, <s>Śūre</s>, <s>Varāgraprāpte</s>, <s>Sāravate</s>,

body.text: svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvadigvidigbhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: may there be well-being for me and all sentient beings from all directions and intermediate directions, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: brahmā cāpy atha śakraś ca lokapālā maheśvarāḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, the world-protectors, the great lords,
all the generals of the <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Hārītī</s> with her children—

children.text: idaṃ puṣpaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca pratigṛhṇantu mamāhutiṃ /
children.translated_text: may they accept this flower and this incense, my oblation;

children.text: vīryeṇa tejasā teṣām aiśvaryeṇa balena ca //
children.translated_text: by their vigor, splendor, sovereignty, and strength,

body.text: nihatāḥ sarvarogāś ca svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvabhayopadravopasargebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: may all diseases be destroyed! May there be well-being for me and all sentient beings from all fears, calamities, and afflictions, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottama /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O hero among men; homage to you, O supreme among men;
we salute you with palms joined—O <s>Dharmarāja</s>, homage to you!

body.text: vātajāḥ pittajā rogāḥ śleṣmajāḥ sannipātajāḥ / nihatāḥ sarvarogāś ca svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvabhayopadravopasargopāyāsebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: Diseases born of wind, born of bile, born of phlegm, born of the combination of all three humors—may all diseases be destroyed! May there be well-being for me and all sentient beings from all fears, calamities, afflictions, and troubles, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: atha bhagavān etad avocat /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>) spoke thus:

body.text: naikarājasyārthāya buddhā bhagavanto loka utpadyante / naikanagaranigamajanapadagrāmakulānāṃ yāvan naikasatvasyārthāya buddhā bhagavanto loka utpadyante / api tu sadevakasya lokasyārthāya samārakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurāyā buddhā bhagavanto loka utpadyante / tadyathā / syād vaidyaś cikitsakaḥ paramācāryaḥ kuśalo bhiṣajjñāneṣu śikṣito naikarājasyārthāya naikasatvasyārthāya loka utpadyante / evam eva buddhā bhagavanto loka utpadyante / tat kasya hetoḥ / yasyāṃ diśi buddhā bhagavanto viharanti / na tatra manuṣyāmanuṣyān viheṭhayitavyān manyate / pañcāhaṃ yena vaiśālī mahānagarī tenopasaṃkrāmeyam / evaṃ mayā vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ mahājanakāyasyārthāya kṛto bhaviṣyati buddhakāryaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, do not arise in the world for the sake of one king alone; nor for the sake of one city, market-town, district, village, or clan alone; nor even for the sake of one sentient being alone do the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, arise in the world. Rather, for the sake of the world with its gods, with <s>Māra</s>, with ascetics and Brahmins, for the sake of beings including gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, arise in the world. Just as a physician, a healer, a supreme teacher, skilled and trained in the knowledge of medicine, does not arise in the world for the sake of one king alone, nor for the sake of one sentient being alone—even so do the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, arise in the world. For what reason? In whatever direction the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, dwell, there one should not think of harming humans or non-humans. In five days I shall proceed to where the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> is. Thus shall I have accomplished the <s>Buddha</s>'s work for the sake of the great assembly at <s>Vaiśālī</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān pūrvāhṇakālasamaye nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāyārdhatrayodaśabhir bhikṣuśataiḥ sārdhaṃ gṛdhrakūṭāt parvatād avatīrṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken his robe and bowl, descended from <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain together with twelve hundred and fifty monks.

body.text: atha brahmā sahāpatiḥ pañcamātrāṇi divyāni chatraśatāny ādāya bhagavato dakṣiṇeṇopanāmitavān / upanāmya bhagavantam
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, taking five hundred divine parasols, offered them to the right side of the Blessed One; and having offered them, he stood

body.text: eva vijayamānaḥ sthito 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: fanning the Blessed One.

body.text: śakro 'pi devānām indraḥ pañcamātrāṇi chatraśatāny ādāya bhagavato vāmenopanāmitavān / upanāmya bhagavantam eva vijayamānaḥ sthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods (<s>Indra</s>), also taking five hundred divine parasols, offered them to the left side of the Blessed One; and having offered them, he stood fanning the Blessed One.

body.text: catvāro 'pi mahārājānaḥ ekaiko 'pi divyāni pañcamātrāṇi chatraśatāny ādāya bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhata upanāmitavanta upanāmya bhagavantam eva vijayamānaḥ sthitaḥ //
body.translated_text: The four great kings also, each taking five hundred divine parasols, offered them behind the Blessed One; and having offered them, they stood fanning the Blessed One.

body.text: maheśvaro 'pi devaputro 'ṣṭāviṃśatiś ca mahāyakṣasenāpatayo dvātriṃśac ca mahāyakṣanagnā hārītī ca saputrikā saparivārā śrāvakānāṃ pratyekaṃ divyaṃ chatram upanāmitavatī vijayantī ca sthitā //
body.translated_text: <s>Maheśvara</s> the divine prince, twenty-eight great <s>Yakṣa</s> generals, thirty-two great naked <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Hārītī</s> with her children and retinue offered a divine parasol to each of the disciples, and stood fanning them.

body.text: evaṃrūpayośolābhasatkārāgraprāpto bhagavān sabhikṣusaṃgho gṛdhrakūṭāt parvatād avatīrya yena vaiśālī mahānagarī tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / adrakṣuḥ khalu punar vaiśālikā licchavayo bhagavantaṃ dūrata evāgacchantaṃ prāsādikaṃ prāsādanīyaṃ śāntendriyaṃ śāntamānasaṃ dāntendriyaṃ dāntamānasaṃ paramottamadamaśamathaprāptaṃ jitendriyaṃ nāgam iva sudāntaṃ hradam ivācchaṃ viprasannam anāvilaṃ dvātriṃśadbhir mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtagātram aśītibhiś cānuvyañjanaiḥ saṃkusumitaṃ vicitritaṃ gātraṃ tathāgatasya śarīraṃ śālarājeva supuṣpitaḥ sūryo vā divā pramuktaraśmijālaḥ / rātrau cāndhakāratamiśrāyāṃ giriśikharagataḥ / prajvālan mahān agniskandhaḥ / mahān iva cāmīkarācaladharaḥ / evam eva bhagavān bhāṣate tapati virocate sahadarśanād eva vaiśālikā licchavayo bhagavato 'ntike cetāṃsi prasādayāmāsuḥ //
body.translated_text: Having thus attained the foremost gain of honor and reverence of such a nature, the Blessed One, together with the assembly of monks, descended from <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain and proceeded to the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>. And the <s>Licchavī</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> beheld the Blessed One approaching from afar—pleasing, inspiring confidence, his senses calmed, his mind calmed, his senses tamed, his mind tamed, having attained supreme and ultimate restraint and tranquility, his senses conquered, tamed like an elephant, clear as a lake, serene, undisturbed, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> decorated and embellished with the eighty minor marks, like a <s>śāla</s> tree in full bloom, like the sun in daytime with its net of rays released, and at night in the midst of dense darkness, stationed on a mountain peak, like a great blazing mass of fire, like a great bearer of a golden mountain. Even so, the Blessed One shone, blazed, and radiated; and at the very sight of him, the <s>Licchavī</s> people of <s>Vaiśālī</s> generated faith in their hearts toward the Blessed One.

body.text: te prasannacittā yena mārgeṇa bhagavān vaiśālīṃ mahānagarīṃ praviśati taṃ mārgaṃ śodhayanti sma / saṃmārjayanti sma / puṣpāvakīrṇaṃ ca vareṇyaṃ kurvanti sma / ucchritavicitrapaṭṭadāmaghaṇṭāchatradhvajapatākānānāgandhāni dhūpitaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāmanti sma / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādayoḥ śirāṃsi nipātayanti //
body.translated_text: They, with minds gladdened, swept and cleaned the road by which the Blessed One was entering the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>; they strewed it with flowers, making it excellent; having raised various colored cloths, festoon-garlands, bells, parasols, banners, and pennants, and perfumed it with various incenses, they approached the Blessed One and placed their heads at his feet.

body.text: atha bhagavān sahasrāracakraruciracaraṇavilikhitatalena padmabimbagarbhasūkumāreṇa pūrvasucaritalakṣaṇopacitena taruṇadivākarakiraṇātirekaprabheṇa / prasṛtabahuraśmiśatasahasranirmalena kareṇa teṣāṃ licchavīnāṃ śirāṃśi parimārjyotthāpya samanuśāsayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, with his hand—whose soles were inscribed by the beautiful thousand-spoked wheel, delicate as the interior of a lotus bud, enriched by the marks of previous good deeds, with a radiance surpassing the rays of the young sun, immaculate with hundreds of thousands of extended rays—wiped the heads of those <s>Licchavīs</s>, raised them up, and instructed them:

body.text: mā bhaiṣṭha mā bhaiṣṭha āryā ethāham abhyāgato yuṣmākam evānukaṃpām upādāya anuttaraṃ jñānam abhisaṃbuddho 'smi / sarvasatvānāṃ ca hitāya sukhāya //
body.translated_text: 'Fear not, fear not, noble ones! Rise! I have come for the sake of compassion for you. Having awakened to supreme knowledge, I am here for the welfare and happiness of all sentient beings.'

body.text: atha bhagavān vaiśālīm mahānagarīṃ praviśya madhyame yāme indrakīlam avaṣṭabhya caturdiśam avalokya suvarṇavarṇabāhuṃ prasāryottarāsaṅgaṃ vicaritvovāca / ye kecit paścime kāle paścime samaye sarṣapaphalamātraṃ tathāgatasya śarīradhātuṃ pūjayiṣyanti / imāṃ ca mahāsāhasrapramardanīṃ vidyārājñīṃ sarvagrahaparimocanīyaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ gaṅgāsikatāprakhyānāṃ tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ buddhamudrāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā udgṛhīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti deśayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti / teṣāṃ sarvatra iti bhayopadravopasargopāyāsāvairakalikalahabandhanavigrahavivādā antaśaḥ paiśūnyapāpakā akuśalā duḥkhadharmā na kramiṣyanti / ajayāś ca bhaviṣyanti sarvaviheṭhakebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having entered the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, at the middle watch of the night, leaning against the <s>Indrakīla</s> (Indra's pillar), surveying the four directions, extending his arm golden in color, adjusting his upper robe, spoke: 'Whoever in the future time, in the final age, shall worship even a mustard-seed-sized relic of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body, and shall take up, retain, recite, teach, and master this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī Vidyārājñī</s>—the <s>dharma</s>-discourse that liberates from all planetary seizures, the <s>Buddha</s>-seal of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>—whether monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen—upon them, nowhere shall fears, calamities, afflictions, troubles, enmities, quarrels, disputes, bonds, conflicts, contentions, or even slander, evil, unwholesome, and painful things encroach; and they shall be unconquerable by all who would harm them.'

body.text: evam ukte brahmā sahāpatir bhagavantam etad avocat /
body.translated_text: When this was spoken, <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> said to the Blessed One:

body.text: katamā ca sā bhadanta bhagavan mahāsāhasrapramardanī nāma vidyārājñī sarvagrahaparimocanīyaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ gaṅgāsikatāprakhyānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ buddhamudrā //
body.translated_text: 'Venerable lord, Blessed One, what is that <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī Vidyārājñī</s>—the <s>dharma</s>-discourse that liberates from all planetary seizures, the <s>Buddha</s>-seal of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>?'

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān brahmāṇaṃ sahāpatim etad avocat /
body.translated_text: When this was spoken, the Blessed One said to <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>:

body.text: tena hi tvaṃ brahman śṛṇu sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru bhāṣiṣya hanta / eva bhadanteti brahmā sahāpatir bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīd bhagavāṃs tasyaitad avocat /
body.translated_text: 'Then, O <s>Brahmā</s>, listen well and carefully, attend to it in your mind, and I shall speak.' 'So be it, Venerable Lord,' <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said to him:

body.text: syād yathedaṃ /
body.translated_text: 'Let it be thus:''

body.text: acale macale / sāramacale / prakṛtivarṇa / prakṛtinirghoṣe / samantamukhe / sthire sthāvare / vighuṣṭaśabde / pragalane / pāraṅgame / sāravarṇe / sāraṅgavate / bale / mahābale / mahānirbhāse svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Acale</s>, <s>Macale</s>, <s>Sāramacale</s>, <s>Prakṛtivarṇa</s>, <s>Prakṛtinirghoṣe</s>, <s>Samantamukhe</s>, <s>Sthire</s>, <s>Sthāvare</s>, <s>Vighuṣṭaśabde</s>, <s>Pragalane</s>, <s>Pāraṅgame</s>, <s>Sāravarṇe</s>, <s>Sāraṅgavate</s>, <s>Bale</s>, <s>Mahābale</s>, <s>Mahānirbhāse</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: tatredam ucyate kāyagatānusmṛtiḥ śamathavipaśyane / trayaḥ samādhayaḥ / catvāro ṛddhipādāḥ / catvāri samyakprahāṇāni / catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni / catvāri dhyānāni / catvāry āryasatyāni / pañcendriyāṇi / pañcabalāni / ṣaḍanusmṛtayaḥ / saptabodhyaṅgāni / āryāṣṭāṅgā mārgāḥ / navānupūrvavihārasamāpattayaḥ / daśatathāgatabalāni / ekādaśavimuktāyatanāni / dvādaśāṅgapratītyasamutpādaḥ / dvādaśakāradharmacakram / ṣoḍaśākāra anāyānānusmṛtiḥ / aṣṭādaśāveṇikābuddhadharmāḥ / dvācatvāriṃśadakṣarāṇi / iyaṃ sā brahman mahāsāhasrapramardanī nāma mahāvidyārājñī sarvagrahaparimocanīyaṃ sūtraṃ gaṅgāsikatāprakhyānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ buddhamudrā / buddhanirhāraḥ / dharmanirhāraḥ / saṃghanirhāraḥ / brahmanirhāraḥ / indranirhāraḥ / lokapālanirhāraḥ / īśvaranirhāraḥ / satyanirhāraḥ / mārganirhāraḥ / pratītyasamutpādanirhāraḥ / candranirhāraḥ / sūryanirhāraḥ / grahanakṣatranirhāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Herein is spoken: mindfulness of the body, <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight); the three <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations); the four bases of supernatural power; the four right exertions; the four foundations of mindfulness; the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations); the four noble truths; the five faculties; the five powers; the six recollections; the seven factors of awakening; the noble eightfold path; the nine successive abiding attainments; the ten powers of the <s>Tathāgata</s>; the eleven bases of liberation; the twelve-limbed dependent origination; the twelve-aspected turning of the <s>dharma</s>-wheel; the sixteen aspects of mindfulness of breathing; the eighteen special qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>; the forty-two syllables.
