This, O <s>Brahmā</s>, is the great <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī Mahāvidyārājñī</s>—the sūtra that liberates from all planetary seizures, the <s>Buddha</s>-seal of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>: the manifestation of the <s>Buddha</s>, the manifestation of the <s>Dharma</s>, the manifestation of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the manifestation of <s>Brahmā</s>, the manifestation of <s>Indra</s>, the manifestation of the world-protectors, the manifestation of <s>Īśvara</s>, the manifestation of truth, the manifestation of the path, the manifestation of dependent origination, the manifestation of the moon, the manifestation of the sun, the manifestation of the planets and constellations.

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: Let it be thus:

body.text: śāle kasine / vidharaṇi / varāgrasāre / amarṣaṇi / amoghavate / secane nakāli / kāsivare / bharaṇe / karakasakhe / samantaprāpte / sāraprāpte / stambhaprāpte / vajradhare svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Śāle</s>, <s>Kasine</s>, <s>Vidharaṇi</s>, <s>Varāgrasāre</s>, <s>Amarṣaṇi</s>, <s>Amoghavate</s>, <s>Secane</s>, <s>Nakāli</s>, <s>Kāsivare</s>, <s>Bharaṇe</s>, <s>Karakasakhe</s>, <s>Samantaprāpte</s>, <s>Sāraprāpte</s>, <s>Stambhaprāpte</s>, <s>Vajradhare</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyām imāṃ gāthām abhāṣata /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke this verse:

children.text: imasmin lokeṣv imasmin vā punaḥ svargeṣu vā ratnavarāṇi santi /
children.translated_text: 'In these worlds or again in the heavens, there are jewels most excellent;
there is none equal to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the god above gods, the supreme among men.

children.text: tasmād idaṃ ratnavaraṃ praṇītam etena satyena ihāstu svasti /
children.translated_text: Therefore this supreme jewel is most excellent—by this truth, may there be well-being here!

children.text: kṣayo virāgo hy amṛtaṃ tv asaṃskṛtam ājñāya sauśākyamuniprabhāvitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Cessation, dispassion, the deathless, the unconditioned—having realized [this], proclaimed by the power of the sage of the <s>Śākyas</s>;

body.text: dharmeṇa tena na samo 'sti kaścid amṛtena śāntena asaṃśkṛtena /
body.translated_text: there is nothing equal to that <s>Dharma</s>—the deathless, the peaceful, the unconditioned.

body.text: tasmād idaṃ ratnavaraṃ praṇītam etena satyena ihāstu svasti //
body.translated_text: Therefore this supreme jewel is most excellent—by this truth, may there be well-being here!

children.text: yac chreṣṭham iṣṭaṃ vidhivatprakāśitaṃ śāstā sadānuttarayogavāhakam /
children.translated_text: That which is the best, the desired, rightly proclaimed, the teacher's [gift]—ever the unsurpassed vehicle of yoga;

children.text: samādhinā tena samo na vidyate vajropamenādvayamārgadarśinā //
children.translated_text: there is none equal to that <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), diamond-like, showing the non-dual path.

children.text: tasmād idaṃ ratnavaraṃ praṇītam etena satyena ihāstu svasti /
children.translated_text: Therefore this supreme jewel is most excellent—by this truth, may there be well-being here!

children.text: aṣṭau mahāpudgalaye praśastāḥ khyātāni catvāri yugāni caiva //
children.translated_text: The eight great persons are praised, and the four pairs are renowned.

children.text: te dakṣiṇīyā sugatena gītā maharṣiṇā hy apratipudgalena /
children.translated_text: They are declared worthy of offerings by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), the great sage without equal.

children.text: ebhyaḥ pradānaṃ bhavate mahāphalaṃ bījāni nyastāni yathā sukṣetre //
children.translated_text: Gifts given to them bear great fruit, like seeds sown in a good field.

children.text: idaṃ praṇītaṃ varasaṃgharatnam etena satyena ihāstu svasti /
children.translated_text: This is the supreme jewel of the <s>Saṅgha</s>—by this truth, may there be well-being here!

children.text: ye suprasannāmanasā dṛḍhena upasaṃkramī gautamaśāsanaṃ hi //
children.translated_text: Those who with minds well-gladdened and firm have approached the teaching of <s>Gautama</s>—

children.text: te prāptiprāptā amṛtaṃ vigāhya tamonudā nirvṛtim āpnuvanti /
children.translated_text: they, having attained attainment, plunging into the deathless, dispelling darkness, reach <s>nirvṛti</s> (nirvāṇa).

children.text: idaṃ praṇītaṃ varasaṃgharatnam etena satyena ihāstu svasti //
children.translated_text: This excellent jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> (community) has been set forth; by this truth, may there be well-being here.

children.text: sahasrayogād iha darśanasya trayaḥ prahīṇā yugapat kileśāḥ /
children.translated_text: By the thousand-fold power of this vision, three <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are simultaneously abandoned:

children.text: satkāyadṛṣṭir vicikitsā ca śīlaṃ vrataṃ darśanam āryatā ca //
children.translated_text: <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable aggregate), doubt, and attachment to rules and vows, the vision, and noble status.

children.text: idaṃ praṇītaṃ varasaṃgharatnam etena satyena ihāstu svasti /
children.translated_text: This excellent jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> has been set forth; by this truth, may there be well-being here.

children.text: na jātu kuryāt trividhaṃ hi pādaṃ kāyena vācā manasātha vāpi //
children.translated_text: Never would they commit a threefold transgression, whether by body, speech, or mind.

children.text: prachādanīyaṃ sahasā na kṛtvā yathā na dṛṣṭir grahaṇena teṣām /
children.translated_text: Having not done what should be concealed rashly, just as their view does not involve grasping of those.

children.text: idaṃ praṇītaṃ varasaṃgharatnam etena satyena ihāstu svasti //
children.translated_text: This excellent jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> has been set forth; by this truth, may there be well-being here.
Just as <s>Indra's</s> pillar, established upon the earth, is unshakable by winds from the four directions,

children.text: tathopamā pudgalāḥ santi saṃghe yā āryamārgasya darśinaḥ //
children.translated_text: so too are those persons in the <s>Saṃgha</s> who are seers of the Noble Path.

children.text: idaṃ praṇītaṃ varasaṃgharatnam etena satyena ihāstu svasti /
children.translated_text: This excellent jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> has been set forth; by this truth, may there be well-being here.
Those who discern the Noble Truths, well-taught by one of profound wisdom,

body.text: kāyapradānaṃ ca manasy akṛtvā na te bhayaṃ kaṣṭam avāpnuvanti /
body.translated_text: even without placing in mind the giving up of the body, they do not experience terrible fear.

body.text: idaṃ praṇītaṃ varasaṃgharatnam etena satyena ihāstu svasti //
body.translated_text: This excellent jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> has been set forth; by this truth, may there be well-being here.

children.text: arcir yathā vāyuvaśād vinaṣṭā astaṃgatā naiva upeti saṃkṣā /
children.translated_text: Just as a flame extinguished by the force of wind, having set, does not attain to any designation,

children.text: tathaiva samyojanaviprayuktā adarśanaṃ yānti hi buddhaputrā //
children.translated_text: even so, the sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, freed from fetters, pass beyond perception.

children.text: idaṃ praṇītaṃ varasaṃgharatnam etena satyena ihāstu svasti /
children.translated_text: This excellent jewel of the <s>Saṃgha</s> has been set forth; by this truth, may there be well-being here.

children.text: ye jaṅgamāś cātra tathaiva sthāvarās te sarvasatvāḥ sukhino bhavantu //
children.translated_text: May all beings here, both moving and stationary, be happy.

children.text: śāstāram agryaṃ naradevapūjyaṃ buddhaṃ namasyetha ihāstu svasti /
children.translated_text: Revere the <s>Buddha</s>, the foremost teacher, worshipped by gods and men; may there be well-being here.

children.text: ye jaṅgamāś cātra tathaiva sthāvarās te sarvasatvāḥ sukhino bhavantu //
children.translated_text: May all beings here, both moving and stationary, be happy.

children.text: śāntaṃ virāgaṃ naradevapūjyaṃ dharmaṃ namasyetha ihāstu svasti /
children.translated_text: Revere the <s>Dharma</s>, peaceful and free from passion, worshipped by gods and men; may there be well-being here.

children.text: ye jaṅgamāś cātra tathaiva sthāvarās te sarvasatvāḥ sukhino bhavantu //
children.translated_text: May all beings here, both moving and stationary, be happy.

children.text: gaṇānam agryaṃ naradevapūjyaṃ saṃghaṃ namasyetha ihāstu svasti /
children.translated_text: Revere the <s>Saṃgha</s>, foremost of assemblies, worshipped by gods and men; may there be well-being here.

children.text: yānīha bhūtāni samāgatāni sthitāni bhūmāv atha vāntarīkṣe //
children.translated_text: Whatever beings have assembled here, whether stationed on the earth or in the sky,

children.text: kurvantu maitrī satataṃ prajāsu divā ca rātrau ca carantu dharmam /
children.translated_text: may they constantly practice loving-kindness toward all creatures, and may they practice the <s>Dharma</s> by day and by night.

children.text: yenaiva satyena jino jitāriḥ sa satyavādī ripus tasya nāsti //
children.translated_text: By that very truth by which the Conqueror (<s>Jina</s>) conquered his enemies—he who speaks truth, for him there is no foe—

body.text: tenaiva satyena ihāstu svasti mucyantu sarve 'dya mahābhayebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: by that very truth, may there be well-being here; may all be freed today from great dangers. <s>Svāhā</s>!

body.text: syād yathedam //
body.translated_text: Let it be thus:

body.text: dhire dhidhire / balanirghoṣe / balasāre / sāravate / stute / prabhūtaprāpte / āradhe / āraghoṣe / sāravati / acyute / balavate / śūraprāpte / sāraṃgame / sūryagame / sūryanirghoṣe svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>dhire dhidhire / balanirghoṣe / balasāre / sāravate / stute / prabhūtaprāpte / āradhe / āraghoṣe / sāravati / acyute / balavate / śūraprāpte / sāraṃgame / sūryagame / sūryanirghoṣe svāhā</s>

body.text: iyaṃ sā mahābrahman mahāsāhasrapramardanī nāma vidyārājñī sarvagrahaparimocanīyaṃ sūtraṃ gaṅgāsikatāprakhyānāṃ tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ buddhamudrā / buddhapadā / dharmapadā / saṃghapadā / brahmapadā / indrapadā / lokapālapadā /
body.translated_text: This, O great <s>Brahman</s>, is the <s>vidyā-rājñī</s> (queen of spells) named <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> for the liberation from all seizures, the <s>Buddha</s>-seal of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, and Perfectly Awakened Ones as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>: the <s>Buddha</s>-step, the <s>Dharma</s>-step, the <s>Saṃgha</s>-step, the <s>Brahma</s>-step, the <s>Indra</s>-step, the World-protector-step,

body.text: īśvarapadā / mahārṣipadā / paryarthipadā / āyatipadā / akṣipadā / hetupadā / pradeśapadā / nirdeśapadā / abhisaṃbuddhapadā / samyaksaṃbuddhaiś ca pratyekabuddhaiś ca sparśitā / śrāvakair adhiṣṭhitā / brahmabhiḥ praśaṃsitā / indreṇa pūjitā / lokapālair namaskṛtā / īśvareṇa pūjitā / sarvadevair varṇitā / yogācārair abhinanditā / ṛṣibhir alaṃkṛtā / brahmabhir abistutā / devatābhiś cintitā / snātakaiḥ praśaṃsitā / cāturvarṇena lokena / gocaraḥ sarvabuddhānām / udyānaṃ pratyekabuddhānām / niryāṇaṃ śrāvakānām / āśrayo yogācārāṇām / ākaro bodhipakṣāṇāṃ dharmāṇām / pravāhanaṃ saṃkleśānām / utpāṭanam anuśayaśalyānām / saṃdarśanaṃ mokṣadvārāṇām / bhedanaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭīnām / prapātanaṃ mānaparvatasya / vivaraṇam āryamārgasya / pithanaṃ mokṣadvārāṇām / saṃśoṣaṇaṃ saṃsārasamudrasya / uccālanaṃ sarvasaṃsārapatitānām asthiparvatānām / cchedanī mārapāśasya / uttrāsanī māraparṣadaḥ / udgilanī mārabaḍiśasya / uttrāsanī kleśasaṃgrāmāt / praveśanī nirvāṇanagare / niṣkrāmaṇī saṃsāragṛhād iti //
body.translated_text: the <s>Īśvara</s>-step, the great-sage-step, the seeker-step, the future-step, the eye-step, the cause-step, the indication-step, the exposition-step, the fully-awakened-step; touched by Perfectly Awakened Ones and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; sustained by <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers); praised by <s>Brahmā</s>-gods; worshipped by <s>Indra</s>; honored by the World-protectors; worshipped by <s>Īśvara</s>; extolled by all gods; celebrated by <s>yogācāras</s> (practitioners of yoga); adorned by <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages); hymned by <s>Brahmā</s>-gods; contemplated by deities; praised by the learned; by the world of the four castes; the domain of all <s>Buddhas</s>; the garden of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; the departure-point of <s>Śrāvakas</s>; the refuge of <s>yogācāras</s>; the mine of the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>); the sweeping away of defilements; the uprooting of the thorns of latent tendencies; the revealing of the gates of liberation; the breaking of views regarding the perishable aggregate; the toppling of the mountain of pride; the opening of the Noble Path; the closing of the gates of liberation; the drying up of the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>; the dislodging of the mountains of bones of all those fallen into <s>saṃsāra</s>; the cutter of <s>Māra's</s> snare; the terrifier of <s>Māra's</s> assembly; the disgorger of <s>Māra's</s> hook; the terrifier from the battle of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions); the gateway into the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; the exit from the house of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: Let it be thus:

body.text: khaṅge / khaṅgaghoṣe / uṣodhane / sārathiprabhede / vipulaprabhe / saṃkarṣaṇi / vikarṣaṇi / viṣāgravati / śuddhasādhane / varuṇavate / vāśane / vibhūṣaṇi / viṣaṃgame / paśupati / puṣpagarbhe / svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvabhayopadravopasargopāyāsebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>khaṅge / khaṅgaghoṣe / uṣodhane / sārathiprabhede / vipulaprabhe / saṃkarṣaṇi / vikarṣaṇi / viṣāgravati / śuddhasādhane / varuṇavate / vāśane / vibhūṣaṇi / viṣaṃgame / paśupati / puṣpagarbhe / svāhā</s>—may there be well-being for me and for all beings, from all fears, calamities, afflictions, and distresses. <s>Svāhā</s>!

body.text: iyaṃ sā mahābrahman mahāsāhasrapramardanī nāma vidyārājñī sarvagrahapramocanīyaṃ sūtraṃ gaṅgāsikatāprakhyānāṃ tathāgatānām arhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ buddhamudrā / yayā mudrayā mudritaḥ sadevamānuṣāsuro loko 'nuttaranirvāṇapuraṃ praviṣṭaḥ / yasya cārthāya gaṅgāsikatāprakhyaiḥ samyaksaṃbuddaiḥ pratyekabuddhaiḥ śrāvakaiś ca pūrvābhisaṃbuddhaiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ pratyekabuddhāḥ śrāvakāś ca mātāpitṛdakṣiṇīyā gurusthānīyāḥ paryupāsitā brahmacaryaṃ cīrṇaṃ śīlaṃ rakṣitaṃ
body.translated_text: This, O great <s>Brahman</s>, is the <s>vidyā-rājñī</s> (queen of spells) named <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> for the liberation from all seizures, the <s>Buddha</s>-seal of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, and Perfectly Awakened Ones as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>—the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse by which seal the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> has been sealed and entered the city of unsurpassed <s>Nirvāṇa</s>; for the sake of which, by Perfectly Awakened Ones, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, who had previously attained full awakening, the Perfectly Awakened Ones, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s>—worthy of offerings to parents and occupying the place of teachers—were attended upon, the holy life was practiced, moral discipline was guarded,

body.text: dānaṃ dattaṃ kṛpā pāramitā paripūriḥ / sādhitā bodhisatvacaryā sādhitā bodhiprāptiprāptā sarvajñatā parājito māraḥ //
body.translated_text: gifts were given, compassion and the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) were fulfilled; the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practice was accomplished, the attainment of awakening was reached, omniscience was obtained, and <s>Māra</s> was defeated.

body.text: atha brahmā sahāpatiḥ śakraś ca devānām indraś catvāraś ca mahārājāna ekavāgekamataikasvarā bhagavantaṃ namasyamānā ūcuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and the four Great Kings, with one voice, one mind, and one tone, paying homage to the Blessed One, said:

body.text: aho vidyā mahāvidyā mahāsāhasrapramardanī //
body.translated_text: 'Oh, the <s>vidyā</s> (spell)! The great <s>vidyā</s>! The <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī</s>!

children.translated_text: A protection for all beings, the <s>Buddha</s>-seals in the four directions.
We shall bestow our seal upon this <s>Sāhasrapramardanī Sūtra</s>.
By this seal with which they are sealed, all beings are terrified.

children.text: ye manuṣyā praduṣṭāś ca trasannāś cātra śāsane //
children.translated_text: Those humans who are hostile and who tremble at this teaching—

children.text: teṣāṃ daṇḍaṃ praṇeṣyāmi vidyāṃ brahmeṇa nirmitām /
children.translated_text: upon them I shall bring punishment through this <s>vidyā</s> fashioned by <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: śakreṇa dhāritā mudrā lokapālaiś ca mudritāḥ //
children.translated_text: The seal has been held by <s>Śakra</s>, and sealed by the World-protectors.'

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: Let it be thus:

body.text: kaliṅge / bhārade / jūdagre / jāmale / siṃhamade / sārāgraprāpte / haṃsagāmini / mālini / hule mihule / pihule 2 pihulame haham haham haham haham / sūdani varāgravati / hastine / necaramati / caṇḍāli / carame / carācare svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>kaliṅge / bhārade / jūdagre / jāmale / siṃhamade / sārāgraprāpte / haṃsagāmini / mālini / hule mihule / pihule pihule pihulame haham haham haham haham / sūdani varāgravati / hastine / necaramati / caṇḍāli / carame / carācare svāhā</s>

body.text: asyāṃ khalu punar mahāsāhasrapramardanyāṃ vidyārājñyāṃ bhāṣyamānāyām ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsahasro lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍadhikāram akampat / dikṣu vidikṣu bhūtāśatair yakṣarākṣasair nirnādaḥ prakruṣṭaghoṣaṃ codghoṣayanti sma //
body.translated_text: When this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī vidyā-rājñī</s> (queen of spells) was being spoken, this great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasra lokadhātu</s>) trembled six times. In the directions and intermediate directions, hundreds of <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s> raised a resounding cry and uttered a loud proclamation:

children.text: aho duḥkhamaho kaṣṭaṃ naṣṭā bhūtagaṇā vayam /
children.translated_text: 'Oh, the suffering! Oh, the misery! We hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits) are destroyed!

children.text: vinaṣṭā bhūtasaṃghās tā vaśanītāś ca sarvathā //
children.translated_text: The assemblies of <s>bhūtas</s> are annihilated and completely subjugated.
Powerless now are all our restraints upon living beings.

children.text: te ca bhūmau nipīḍanti saṃprapadyanti duḥkhitāḥ //
children.translated_text: They are pressed down upon the ground, miserable, and they surrender.'

children.text: atha bhagavāṃs tāṃ bhūmīṃ vajramayīm abhinirmimīte /
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One created the ground to be made of <s>vajra</s> (diamond).

children.text: te caturdiśaṃ prapalāyanti atha catvāro mahārājānaḥ //
children.translated_text: They fled in the four directions. Then the four Great Kings

body.text: caturdiśaṃ mahān agnijvālāskandham abhinirmitavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: created a great mass of blazing fire in the four directions.

body.text: te cākāśe paridhāvanti //
body.translated_text: They ran about in the sky.

body.text: atha brahmā sahāpatir ayomayam ākāśam abhinirmimīte / te
body.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s> created the sky to be made of iron. They

body.text: ca saptatālamātraṃ vaihāyasaṃ paridhāvanti / atha śakro devānām indro 'siśaraśaktikuntatomaravṛkṣaparvatavṛṣṭīr abhipravarṣati / tena ca samayena samantataḥ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau pañcayakṣaśatasahasrāṇi sannipatitāni vidyāśāpahatāni jvarāveśonmattāni vipīḍanti / bhagavataḥ pādayoḥ śirāṃsi nipatyābruvan //
body.translated_text: ran about in the air to a height of seven palm-trees. Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, rained down showers of swords, arrows, spears, lances, javelins, trees, and mountains. And at that time, throughout the entire <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, five hundred thousand <s>yakṣas</s> had assembled, struck by the curse of the <s>vidyā</s>, afflicted by fever-possession and madness, and they were tormented. Falling with their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they said:

body.text: sarvasatvahitānukampī śramaṇo gautama /
body.translated_text: 'O ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, compassionate toward the welfare of all beings,

body.text: trāyatu naḥ śramaṇo gautama //
body.translated_text: save us, O ascetic <s>Gautama</s>!'

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tān guhyakān maitryā spharanti sma / śikṣāgrahaṇaṃ ca kārayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One suffused those <s>guhyakas</s> (secret beings) with loving-kindness and caused them to accept the precepts:

children.text: yā gatir mātṛghāṭīnāṃ pitṛghāṭīnāṃ ca yā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever is the destiny of those who murder their mothers, and whatever is the destiny of those who murder their fathers,

children.text: arhatāṃ ghāṭakasyāpi saṃghabhedī ca yā gatiḥ //
children.translated_text: and whatever is the destiny of one who slays an <s>Arhat</s>, and of one who causes a schism in the <s>Saṃgha</s>,
and of one with a mind hostile toward the Perfectly Awakened One, and of one who draws blood [from a <s>Tathāgata</s>]—

children.text: tāṃ gatiṃ pratipadyema yadi mudrāṃ kṣipemahi //
children.translated_text: that destiny we shall obtain if we were to violate this seal.
May our heads split into seven pieces, like the flower-cluster of an <s>arjaka</s> plant.
May we be afflicted by the disease of <s>yakṣas</s>, and may our bodies become mottled.
This <s>Sāhasrapramardanī Sūtra</s>, which was spoken by the Conqueror (<s>Jina</s>),
if we transgress this <s>vidyā-rājñī</s> (queen of spells), may we live [only] at our own [peril].'

body.text: tena ca samayena vaiśālyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ sarve iti bhayopadravopasargopāyāsāḥ pratiprasrabdhāḥ / yakṣarākṣasamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ svakasvakaṃ gocaram atikrāntāḥ / vaiśālakā licchavayaś ca sarvarogavyādhibhyo vinirmuktāḥ sarvasukhasamarpitā buddhe 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatā babhūvuḥ / dharme 'vetya prasādena samanvāgatā babhūvuḥ / satatasamitaṃ ratnatrayapūjābhiratā mahotsavena viharantaḥ / haṃsaśukaśārikākokilamayūracakravākakunārajīvañjīvakapakṣigaṇā madhuraṃ nikūjanti sma / vigatakāyapīḍāḥ sāṃsara iva kinnarāḥ / aghāṭitāni ratnabhājanāni raṇanti sma / bherīśaṅkhamṛdaṅgapaṇavavīṇāveṇavaś ca yathā sthāne sthāpitā eva pravādyanti sma / dāḍimabilvāmalanyagrodhāśvatthaprakṣakapitthodumbaraśālatālatamālatilakacampakavṛkṣā nānāgandhān pramuñcanti sma / devatāsahasraiś ca hīhīkārapramuktaḥ / antarīkṣāc ca
body.translated_text: And at that time, in the great city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, all fears, calamities, afflictions, and distresses were pacified. The <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, non-human beings, and humans each returned to their own domains. The <s>Vaiśālikas</s> and the <s>Licchavis</s> were freed from all diseases and ailments, endowed with all happiness, and possessed of unwavering faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, possessed of unwavering faith in the <s>Dharma</s>. Constantly delighting in the worship of the Three Jewels, they dwelt in great festivity. Flocks of geese, parrots, <s>śārikā</s> (myna birds), <s>kokila</s> (cuckoos), peacocks, <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy sheldrakes), <s>kunāra</s>, and <s>jīvañjīvaka</s> birds sang sweetly. Free from bodily affliction, like <s>kinnaras</s> in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Jeweled vessels rang of their own accord. Drums, conches, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, <s>paṇavas</s>, <s>vīṇās</s>, and flutes, placed in their proper positions, played of themselves. Pomegranate, <s>bilva</s>, <s>āmalaka</s> (gooseberry), banyan, <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>prakṣaka</s>, <s>pittha</s>, <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig), <s>śāla</s>, palm, <s>tamāla</s>, <s>tilaka</s>, and <s>campaka</s> trees released various fragrances. And thousands of deities uttered joyful cries. And from the sky

body.text: puṣpavarṣam abhipraviṣṭam / amānuṣaś ca gandho loke prādurbhūtaḥ //
body.translated_text: a rain of flowers descended. And a superhuman fragrance manifested in the world.

body.text: atha catvāro mahārājānaḥ prāñjalayo bhagavantam etad avocat /
body.translated_text: Then the four Great Kings, with palms joined, addressed the Blessed One thus:

body.text: idaṃ bhadanta bhagavan mahāsāhasrapramardanī sūtrarājaṃ sarvagrahapramocanīyaṃ buddhamudrā dharmaparyāyam / yaḥ kaścic chikṣāpadaṃ parigṛhītvā kāśāyadhārī udgṛhya dhārayitvā vācayitvā deśayitvā paryavāpya likhitvā granthayitvā dhārayiṣyati / tasya sarve iti bhayopadravopasargopāyāsāvairakalikalahabhaṇḍanavivādā yāvat paiśūnyakā akuśalā dharmā nābhikramiṣyanti / ajayaś ca bhaviṣyanti sarvaviheṭhakebhyaḥ / tena rāṣṭrasya sīmābandhayitukāmena susnātena triśuklabhuktena pañcāmiṣaparivarjitena sarvamānuṣaśiṣyāpadaparigṛhītena sarvasatvasamācittena vastrābharaṇayuktena grāmanagaranigamaśṛṅgāṭakakulāny apagatasaṃkārakūṭāni kṛtvā madhyamāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ puṣpāvakīrṇāṃ dharaṇīṃ kṛtvā nānāgandhā dhūpayitavyā / caturdiśaṃ catasraḥ kanyakāḥ susnātavibhūṣitāḥ śastrahastāḥ sthāpayitavyāḥ / catvāro ghaṇṭāś catvāri ratnabhājanāni gandhodakapuṣpaphalaparipūrṇāni sthāpayitavyāni / pūrvāhṇakālasamaye udgate sahasrakiraṇavidyā āvartayitavyā / palaṣaṣṭhikayā sūtraṃ kartayitavyaṃ likhitvā cīrikāyāṃ mūrdhni mahācaityeṣu mahāvṛkṣeṣu mahādhvajeṣu cocchrāpayitavyā / nānāpuṣpair nānāgandhaiś ca pakṣamātraṃ pūjā kartavyā / divase divase caikavāraṃ vidyā āvartayitavyā / evaṃ rāṣṭraḥ parimocito bhaviṣyati / evaṃ janapadarājadhānīsthānavihāradevakulakṣatraśālāvṛkṣaphalaharitārāmagośālapaśuśālā apagatasaṃkārāḥ kṛtvā khadirabadarāgniṃ prajvālya puṣpāvakīrṇāṃ dharaṇīṃ kṛtvā dvāraśālaśobhanāṃ nānāgandhapradhūpitāṃ kṛtvā sarvabījāni sarpiṣāṃ mrakṣayitvā caturdiśaṃ prakṣeptavyāni / agnau ca prakṣeptavyāni nānāraṅgāni ca sūtrāṇi dvāre bandhanīyāni tiryagyonigatāni niṣkāsya punaḥ praveśayitavyāni / vidyā cāvartayitavyāni / likhitvā granthayitvā cordhvam utthāpya pūjanīyā / glānasya purato buddhapratibimbaṃ vā
body.translated_text: 'Venerable Sir, Blessed One! This <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī Sūtra-rāja</s> (King of Sūtras), the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse that is the <s>Buddha</s>-seal for the liberation from all seizures—whoever, having accepted the precepts and wearing the ochre robes, masters, retains, recites, teaches, comprehends, copies, binds together, and upholds it, for that person all fears, calamities, afflictions, distresses, enmities, quarrels, disputes, contentions, and slander—all unwholesome states up to and including—shall not assail them. And they shall be unconquerable by all who would cause harm. For one who wishes to bind the boundaries of a kingdom, having bathed well, having eaten the three pure foods, having avoided the five kinds of meat, having accepted all precepts for human disciples, with a mind equal toward all beings, adorned with garments and ornaments, having made the villages, cities, market-towns, crossroads, and households free of refuse-heaps, having strewn the ground with flowers in the central royal capital, various incenses should be burned. In the four directions, four maidens, well-bathed and adorned, holding weapons, should be stationed. Four bells and four jewel-vessels filled with scented water, flowers, and fruits should be placed. At the time of forenoon, when the sun has risen, the <s>vidyā</s> should be recited. The <s>sūtra</s> should be written on a strip of cloth with sixty <s>palas</s> [of ink], and should be raised aloft on the head, at great <s>caityas</s> (shrines), at great trees, and on great banners. Worship with various flowers and various incenses should be performed for a fortnight. Day after day, the <s>vidyā</s> should be recited once. Thus shall the kingdom be protected. Likewise, having made the countryside, royal capitals, settlements, monasteries, temples, assembly halls, trees, orchards of fruits and vegetables, cow-sheds, and animal-sheds free of refuse, having kindled a fire of <s>khadira</s> (acacia) and <s>badara</s> (jujube) wood, having strewn the ground with flowers, having made the gate-halls beautiful, having fumigated with various incenses, all seeds should be anointed with ghee and cast in the four directions; and cast into the fire; and sūtras of various colors should be tied at the door; animals should be driven out and then brought back in; and the <s>vidyā</s> should be recited; and having written and bound it, it should be raised aloft and worshipped. Before a sick person, an image of the <s>Buddha</s> or

body.text: buddhaśarīraṃ vā / samudgatemaṃ cevāpīṭhe vāvaropya brahmapratibimbaṃ vā śakrapratibimbaṃ vā caturmahārājapratibimbaṃ vā catasro mudrāḥ kṛtvā sthāpayitavyāḥ / nānāpuṣpair nānādhūpair nānāgandhair brahmaśakracaturmahārājamaheśvarayakṣasenāpatir yakṣamahānagnā hārītī ca namnā trayāṇāṃ ratnānāṃ pūjā kartavyā / teṣāṃ balenaiśvaryādhipatena ca svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca muñcantu sarvaglānāḥ sarvavyādhibhyaḥ / glānasya cānnapānabhaiṣajyam //
body.translated_text: a <s>Buddha</s> relic; or, having placed it upon a raised seat or pedestal, one should make four <s>mudrās</s> (ritual gestures) and establish an image of <s>Brahmā</s>, or an image of <s>Śakra</s>, or images of the Four Great Kings. With various flowers, various incenses, and various fragrances, worship of the Three Jewels should be performed in the names of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, the Four Great Kings, <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Yakṣasenāpati</s> (general of the <s>Yakṣas</s>), <s>Yakṣa Mahānagnā</s>, and <s>Hārītī</s>. By their power, sovereignty, and lordship, may there be well-being for me and for all beings; may all the sick be released from all diseases. And food, drink, and medicine for the sick—

children.translated_text: while offering these, this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) should be recited:
In the awakening of the fully awakened one, the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-protectors) in the four directions,
having brought four vessels to the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One),
offered them, and the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) fashioned one supreme vessel from them.
The <s>Śāstā</s> (Teacher) took in his hand medicine like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality);
by this true utterance, may the medicine become <s>amṛta</s> (nectar).

children.text: hārītī ca tathā devī gṛhya paśyāṃ tathā śubham /
children.translated_text: And the goddess <s>Hārītī</s>, having taken and beheld that auspicious one,
gave to the Teacher divine medicine like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality).
By this true utterance, may it remove the affliction of the sick;

children.text: sarvam upahāraṃ cāpi bhavatv amṛtam auṣadham //
children.translated_text: may all offerings also become nectarean medicine.
By the spiritual power of <s>Vipaśyin</s> Buddha, and by the strength of <s>Śikhin</s>,
by the true utterance of <s>Viśvabhū</s>, by the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) of <s>Krakucchanda</s>,

children.text: kanakāhvasya jñānena ṛddhyā vai kāśyapasya ca /
children.translated_text: by the knowledge of <s>Kanakamuni</s>, and by the miraculous power of <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
by the heroic energy of <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (the Lion of the Śākyas), may the medicine become <s>amṛta</s> (nectar).
Having made the sick person face east, one should offer the medicine;

children.text: imāṃ pāṇitale vidyāṃ tasmin kāle udāharet //
children.translated_text: at that time, one should recite this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) upon the palm of the hand.

body.text: syād yathedam //
body.translated_text: It is as follows:

body.text: khaṭe / khaṭavikhaṭe / vimale / vilambe / bale balavate / candre / caraṇe / amṛtanirghoṣe svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>khaṭe / khaṭavikhaṭe / vimale / vilambe / bale balavate / candre / caraṇe / amṛtanirghoṣe svāhā</s> //

body.text: vātajāḥ pittajā rogāḥ śleṣmajāḥ sannipātajāḥ / nihatāḥ sarvarogāś ca svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvadā sarvabhayebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: Diseases born of <s>vāta</s> (wind), diseases born of <s>pitta</s> (bile), diseases born of <s>śleṣma</s> (phlegm), and those born of the conjunction of all three—may all diseases be destroyed; may there be well-being for me and for all beings, always, from all fears. <s>Svāhā</s>.

body.text: sarvakākhordavetāḍasaṃprayukteṣu karmasu tena puruṣeṇa striyā vā 'horātro vapuṣṭena susnātena subhūṣitena puṣpāvakīrṇāṃ nānāgandhapradhūpitāṃ ca dharaṇīṃ kṛtvā khadiravadarāgniṃ prajvālya sarvabījāni caturdiśaṃ prakṣeptavyāni / nānāraṅgāni ca sūtrāṇi śastreṣu vā śūleṣu vā kunteṣu vā kāṇḍeṣu vā granthayitvā bandhanīyāni sarvamūlāni sarvapuṣpāṇi nānāgandhodakaṃ kṛtvā mahati kuṇḍe prakṣeptavyāni / yasya kākhordakṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati / tasya taṃ sūtrakam ābandhya kuṇḍe 'dhiṣṭhāpanīyaḥ śastreṇa taṃ sūtrakaṃ cchitvā agnau prakṣeptavyam / idaṃ ca mahāsāhasrapramardanīsūtram udāhartavyam /
body.translated_text: For one wishing to counteract all sorcery, <s>kākhorda</s> (black magic), <s>vetāḍa</s> (zombie sorcery), and related rites: that man or woman, having fasted for a day and night, well-bathed and well-adorned, having prepared a ground strewn with flowers and fumigated with various fragrances, kindling a fire of <s>khadira</s> (acacia) and <s>badara</s> (jujube) wood, should cast all manner of seeds in the four directions. Various colored threads should be tied to weapons—swords, spears, lances, or arrows—and all roots, all flowers, and water infused with various fragrances should be cast into a great pit. For whomever the <s>kākhorda</s> (black magic) has been performed, one should bind that thread upon him, place him over the pit, cut the thread with a weapon, and cast it into the fire. And this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī Sūtra</s> should be recited.

children.text: buddhāḥ pratyekabuddhāś ca buddhānāṃ śrāvakāś ca ye /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and those who are disciples of the <s>Buddhas</s>,
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-protectors), and the lords of the <s>Yakṣa</s> generals,
and likewise <s>Yakṣa Nagnā</s> and <s>Hārītī</s> together with her sons—
by their heroic energy and spiritual power, may the <s>vetāḍa</s> (zombie sorcery) rites be cut asunder.
Diamonds and jewels are split, fire burns fuel,
clouds are dried up by wind, trees by the sun.
By this true utterance, may the <s>kākhorda</s> (black magic) rites be burned away;
by various fragrances and flowers, may all evils be purified.

body.text: tadyathā /
body.translated_text: The formula is:

body.text: hume 2 kakhali / kharali / jukvini / javale / garage / hariṇi / śāvari śānti / prasānti svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>hume hume kakhali / kharali / jukvini / javale / garage / hariṇi / śāvari śānti / prasānti svāhā</s> //

body.text: dhāvani svāhā / pradhāvani svāhā / gāndharve svāhā / palaṅgani svāhā / sarvakākhordakṛtavetāḍacchedani svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>dhāvani svāhā / pradhāvani svāhā / gāndharve svāhā / palaṅgani svāhā / sarvakākhordakṛtavetāḍacchedani svāhā</s> //

body.text: imair mantrapadair mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvakākhordavetāḍauṣadhimantraviṣayogāḥ sarvadevaiś ccheditāḥ parājitāḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: By these <s>mantra</s>-words, may all <s>kākhorda</s> (black magic), <s>vetāḍa</s> (zombie sorcery), herb-spells, <s>mantra</s>-practices, and poison preparations directed against me and all beings be cut and defeated by all the gods. <s>Svāhā</s>.

body.text: galagaṇḍavaisarpātisāronmādagaṇḍapiṭakabhagandaraviṣapītakāt parimocayitukāmena susnātena subhūṣitena bhadrapīṭhāsananiṣaṇṇena iyaṃ vidyā udāhartavyā /
body.translated_text: For one wishing to be freed from goiter, erysipelas, dysentery, madness, boils, abscesses, fistula, and poisoning—having bathed well, adorned well, and seated upon an auspicious seat—this <s>vidyā</s> (spell) should be recited:

children.translated_text: By the spiritual power of all the <s>Buddhas</s>, by the power of the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary victors),
and by the heroic energy of the <s>Arhats</s> (worthy ones) and all bearers of <s>mantras</s>,
by the wisdom of <s>Śāriputra</s>, and by the miraculous power of <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>,
by the divine eye of <s>Aniruddha</s>, and by the ascetic virtues of <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
by the priority of attainment of <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, and by the learning of <s>Ānanda</s>,

children.text: maitryā vai brahmaṇā caiva aiśvaryeṇa śatakratoḥ //
children.translated_text: by the loving-kindness of <s>Brahmā</s> indeed, and by the sovereignty of <s>Śatakratu</s> (Indra),
by the dominions of the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-protectors), and by the power of <s>Maheśvara</s>,
by the valor of the generals, and by the prosperity of <s>Hārītī</s>—

children.text: vīryeṇa tejasā teṣāṃ viṣam astv aviṣaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: by their heroic energy and spiritual power, may poison always become non-poison;
therein these <s>mantra</s>-words become poison-free and poison-destroying.

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: It is as follows:

body.text: harikeśi / nakile / rehile / amare aṇḍare paṇḍare / kaṭake / keyūre / hase hase hase / khase khase khase / kharaṅge / marugahaṇe svāhā // mumukṣa svāhā / hile svāhā / mile svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>harikeśi / nakile / rehile / amare aṇḍare paṇḍare / kaṭake / keyūre / hase hase hase / khase khase khase / kharaṅge / marugahaṇe svāhā // mumukṣa svāhā / hile svāhā / mile svāhā</s> //

children.text: hatā gaṇḍāḥ kilāsāś ca vaisarpāś ca vicarcikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Destroyed are tumors and leprosy, erysipelas and eczema,

children.text: piṭṭakā lohaliṅgāś ca kacchūr bhavati saptamī //
children.translated_text: boils and skin eruptions, and scabies is the seventh.

children.text: rāgo dveṣaś ca mohaś ca ete loke trayo viṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Passion, hatred, and delusion—these are the three poisons in the world;
the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> is free from poison; by the <s>Buddha's</s> spiritual power, poison is destroyed.

children.text: rāgo dveṣaś ca mohaś ca ete loke trayo viṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Passion, hatred, and delusion—these are the three poisons in the world;
the Blessed <s>Dharma</s> is free from poison; by the <s>Dharma's</s> spiritual power, poison is destroyed.

children.text: rāgo dveṣaś ca mohaś ca ete loke trayo viṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Passion, hatred, and delusion—these are the three poisons in the world;
the Blessed <s>Saṃgha</s> is free from poison; by the <s>Saṃgha's</s> spiritual power, poison is destroyed.

children.text: viṣasya pṛthivī mātā viṣasya pṛthivī pitā /
children.translated_text: The earth is the mother of poison, the earth is the father of poison;

children.text: etena satyavākyena viṣāḥ sarve syur nirviṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: by this true utterance, may all poisons become non-poisonous.

body.text: bhūmiṃ saṃkrāmantu viṣaṃ pūrṇapātre vā saṃkrāmantu viṣaṃ svāhā //
body.translated_text: May the poison pass into the earth, or may the poison pass into a full vessel. <s>Svāhā</s>.

body.text: athātaḥ kalikalahavigrahavivādaparacakraśatrūṇy aparājayitukāmena pūrvaṃ mahācaitye pūjā kartavyā / iyaṃ ca mahāsāhasrapramardanī vidyārājñī pravartayitavyā //
body.translated_text: Now then, for one wishing to remain unconquered against strife, quarrel, conflict, dispute, enemy armies, and adversaries, worship should first be performed at a great <s>caitya</s> (shrine), and this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī Vidyārājñī</s> (Queen of Spells) should be set in motion.

children.text: buddhena nirjitā mārā dharmeṇa ca adharmatā /
children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s> was conquered by the <s>Buddha</s>, and unrighteousness by the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: saṃghena nirjitā tīrthyā indreṇa asurā jitāḥ /
children.translated_text: the heretics were conquered by the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the <s>Asuras</s> were defeated by <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: asurais tu jitaḥ somo vainateyena sāgaraḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> was conquered by the <s>Asuras</s>, and the ocean by <s>Vainateya</s> (Garuḍa).

children.text: agninā ca jitāḥ kāṣṭhā udakenāgniḥ parājitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Wood is conquered by fire, fire is defeated by water,
clouds are conquered by wind, and rock is shattered by the diamond-thunderbolt.

children.text: satyena devās tiṣṭhanti satyena pṛthivī sthitā /
children.translated_text: By truth the gods stand firm, by truth the earth is established;

children.text: satyaṃ buddhaś ca dharmaś ca satyaṃ jayatu mā mṛṣāḥ //
children.translated_text: truth is the <s>Buddha</s> and the <s>Dharma</s>; may truth be victorious, not falsehood.

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: It is as follows:

body.text: amṛte agrapuṣpe / bahuphale / nivāriṇi sarvārthasādhani / aparājite / dharadharaṇi / guhyāvarte / gautame / guptamati / jambhani svāhā // balaprabhañjani svāhā // jaye svāhā // vijaye svāhā / jaye vijaye svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>amṛte agrapuṣpe / bahuphale / nivāriṇi sarvārthasādhani / aparājite / dharadharaṇi / guhyāvarte / gautame / guptamati / jambhani svāhā // balaprabhañjani svāhā // jaye svāhā // vijaye svāhā / jaye vijaye svāhā</s> //

children.translated_text: The adversaries are conquered and all evildoers are defeated.

children.text: tato 'tha śāstā sarvajña imāṃ gāthām abhāṣata //
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Śāstā</s> (Teacher), the Omniscient One, spoke this verse:
<s>Akṣobhya</s> the King, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Amitābha</s>, <s>Nemi</s>, <s>Ratna</s>, <s>Arci</s>, <s>Meru</s>,

children.text: vajrasya co nāma gṛhītvā sarvadā naivaṃ bhayaṃ bhonti na chambitatvam //
children.translated_text: and having always taken the name of <s>Vajra</s>, there shall be no fear nor trembling.

children.text: ya eṣān aṣṭān mahādyutīnāṃ nāmāni kīrteya anugrahārtham /
children.translated_text: Whoever recites the names of these eight greatly radiant ones for the sake of blessing,

children.text: na tasya agnir na viṣaṃ na śastraṃ krameṇa kāye kṛta sapavitre //
children.translated_text: neither fire, nor poison, nor weapon shall approach his body, made pure thereby.

children.text: saced asau āghātane upasthite utkṛṣṭaśastre vadhake ca saṃmukham /
children.translated_text: If a violent assault should arise, with a raised weapon and an executioner face to face,

children.text: anusmaranto avalokiteśvaraṃ te khaṇḍakhaṇḍaṃ prapateyuḥ śastrāḥ //
children.translated_text: remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, those weapons would fall shattered to pieces.

children.text: saced udgṛhītaṃ pi bhaveta śastraṃ bhañjitvā pāṇiṃ dharaṇīṃ pateyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Even if a weapon were already seized and raised, it would break and fall from the hand to the ground;

children.text: na tasya kāye nipateya kiṃcid anyatra karma pūrimena yat kṛtam //
children.translated_text: nothing would fall upon his body, except for what was done by previous <s>karma</s> (past actions).

body.text: samagradevā imaṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣiṣuḥ /
body.translated_text: All the gods together spoke this verse:

children.text: namo 'stu te buddha anantagocarā namo 'stu te satyaprakāśakā mune /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O <s>Buddha</s>, whose range is infinite! Homage to you, O <s>Muni</s> (Sage), who illuminates the truth!

children.text: satyaṃ pratiṣṭhāya prajāya mocase sarve ca kāmāḥ saphālā bhavantu //
children.translated_text: Having established truth, you liberate beings; may all wishes be fruitful.

body.text: mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca svāhā //
body.translated_text: For me and for all beings. <s>Svāhā</s>.

children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, the Great <s>Brahmā</s>, arose with palms joined together:
"Well-spoken is this <s>vidyā</s> (spell), the <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī</s> (Great Spell that Crushes a Thousand)!
I shall proclaim a <s>vidyā</s> (spell) that brings benefit to children.
I pay homage to the heroic <s>Buddha</s>, the King of <s>Dharma</s>, the maker of auspiciousness,
by whom the <s>vidyā</s> (spell) was first illuminated in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> (the Rose-Apple Continent),

children.text: dharmāya ca viśiṣṭhāya saṃghāya ca gaṇottame //
children.translated_text: and to the excellent <s>Dharma</s>, and to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, the supreme assembly."

children.text: buddhasya pādau vanditvā brahmā vacanam abravīt /
children.translated_text: Having bowed at the feet of the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke these words:

children.text: buddhāḥ pratyekabuddhāś ca buddhānāṃ śrāvakāś ca ye //
children.translated_text: "The <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and those who are disciples of the <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: ṛṣayo lokapālāś ca yāvanto devatāpi ca /
children.translated_text: the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages), the <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-protectors), and as many deities as there are—
all these have arisen from this human world.
There are here terrible <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons) who attack the womb, O Great Sage;

children.text: śakyo na te 'pi ca draṣṭuṃ nāpi śakyāś caturdiśam //
children.translated_text: they cannot even be seen, nor can they be warded off in the four directions.

children.text: yāsāṃ putro na jāyante yāsāṃ garbho na tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: For those women whose sons are not born, for those whose embryo does not remain,
through the union of man and woman, the senses become confused.
They destroy the seed of offspring, whether at the embryonic stage or the bubble stage;

children.text: niṣpannā garbhayā ca strī jāyate na viśalyate //
children.translated_text: and a woman whose pregnancy has matured gives birth but does not recover.

children.text: nāmāni teṣām ākhyāse lokanātha śṛṇohi me /
children.translated_text: I shall declare their names—O Protector of the World, listen to me!
<s>Mañjuka</s>, <s>Mṛgarāja</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Apasmāra</s>, <s>Muṣṭikā</s>,

children.text: mātṛkā jāmikaś caiva kāminī revatī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Mātṛkā</s>, <s>Jāmika</s>, <s>Kāminī</s>, <s>Revatī</s> likewise,
<s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Mātṛnandā</s>, <s>Śakunī</s>, and <s>Kaṇṭhapāṇinī</s>,
<s>Mukhamaṇḍikā</s> and <s>Ālambā</s>—they roam the entire earth.
These are the fifteen <s>grahas</s> (seizing demons) who bring terror to children.
I shall describe their signs, forms, and the manner in which they seize children:
When seized by <s>Mañjuka</s>, the eyes roll about;
when seized by <s>Mṛgarāja</s>, there is terrible vomiting;
when seized by <s>Skanda</s>, the child's shoulders tremble;

children.text: apasmāragṛhītas tu pheṇaṃ lālāṃ ca muñcati /
children.translated_text: when seized by <s>Apasmāra</s>, the child emits foam and saliva;
when seized by <s>Muṣṭikā</s>, the fists clench and do not open;

body.text: mātṛkāsaṃgṛhītasya stanate hasate tathā /
body.translated_text: when seized by <s>Mātṛkā</s>, the child cries out and also laughs;

body.text: jāmikāsaṃgṛhītas tu nābhinandati sa stanau //
body.translated_text: when seized by <s>Jāmikā</s>, the child does not delight in the breast;

children.translated_text: when seized by <s>Kāminī</s>, the child cries out while sleeping;
when seized by <s>Revatī</s>, the child bites the tongue with the teeth;
when seized by <s>Pūtanā</s>, the child coughs and also howls;
when seized by <s>Mātṛnandā</s>, the child displays various strange forms;
when seized by <s>Śakunī</s>, a foul stench emanates;
when seized by <s>Kaṇṭhapāṇī</s>, the throat becomes constricted;
when seized by <s>Mukhamaṇḍī</s>, there is fever and purging;
when seized by <s>Ālambā</s>, hiccups and labored breathing arise.

children.text: tatra rūpaṃ samākhyāsye yathā trāsyanti dārakān /
children.translated_text: Now I shall describe the forms in which they terrify children:
<s>Mañjuka</s> in the form of a cow, <s>Mṛgarāja</s> in the form of a deer,
<s>Skanda</s> in the form of a youth, <s>Apasmāra</s> like a jackal,
<s>Muṣṭikā</s> in the form of a crow, <s>Mātṛkā</s> in the form of a goat,
<s>Jāmikā</s> in the form of a horse, <s>Kāminī</s> in the form of a cowherd,
<s>Revatī</s> in the form of a dog, <s>Pūtanā</s> in the form of a pig,
<s>Mātṛnandā</s> as a cat, <s>Śakunī</s> in the form of a bird,
<s>Kaṇṭhapāṇī</s> as a rooster, <s>Mukhamaṇḍikā</s> as an owl,
<s>Ālambā</s> in the form of a vulture—these terrify children.
These terrible ones steal the vital essence and bring terror to children.
I shall bring them together, dragged by the noose of this <s>sūtra</s> (scripture).
<s>Candana</s> is the name of the <s>Gandharva</s>, the great general of the <s>Yakṣas</s>;

children.text: tasya lekhaṃ ca mudrāṃ ca datvā dūtyena preṣayet /
children.translated_text: having given him a written command and a seal, one should dispatch him as a messenger:

children.text: ugrān grantha samānehi tvaṃ tān pañcadaśān grahān //
children.translated_text: 'Bring those fifteen <s>grahas</s> (seizing demons) here swiftly, bound firmly!'
By him they are instantly brought, tormented by fivefold bonds.
Then the Great <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to the Protector of the World with palms joined:

children.text: etāni tāni bhūtāni bījaṃ nāśenti prāṇinām /
children.translated_text: 'These are the beings that destroy the seed of living creatures;
I shall pronounce their punishment in the presence of the Protector of the World.

children.text: yasyā na jāyate putro jāto vā yasya gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: For her whose son is not born, or for him whose child is seized—
the disciple following the true <s>Dharma</s> should observe the eighth and fourteenth days,

body.text: caityaṃ saṃpūjayitvā tu susnātāḥ suvibhūṣitāḥ /
body.translated_text: and having worshipped at a <s>caitya</s> (shrine), well-bathed and well-adorned,

body.text: sarṣapāliptadharaṇīṃ puṣpagandhasamākulāḥ //
body.translated_text: on ground anointed with mustard seeds, covered with flowers and fragrances,

children.translated_text: one should have a hundred knots tied with a five-colored thread.

children.text: ardharātre sthite kāle mūṣṭiṃ sthitvā tu sarṣapān //
children.translated_text: At the time of midnight, standing firm, holding mustard seeds in the fist,

children.text: brahmanirmitam ity āhur brahmaṇā ca prakaṃpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: one should declare it to be created by <s>Brahmā</s>, and by <s>Brahmā</s> they are made to tremble.
This is beneficial for children up to twelve years of age.

children.text: yo imām atikramed vidyāsūtraṃ brahmaṇā nirmitām /
children.translated_text: Whoever would transgress this <s>vidyā</s>-thread created by <s>Brahmā</s>,
his head shall split into seven pieces, like the flower-cluster of the <s>Arjaka</s> plant.'"

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: It is as follows:

body.text: aṅge vaṅge bhaṅge / bhavane / inandi vinandi / mulali / giri / garari / garuṇi / śaruṇi / girigavare / locane / roṣaṇe / lasane / rocane / alabhe / aṅgane / alaphe talaphe / prakarṣaṇi svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>aṅge vaṅge bhaṅge / bhavane / inandi vinandi / mulali / giri / garari / garuṇi / śaruṇi / girigavare / locane / roṣaṇe / lasane / rocane / alabhe / aṅgane / alaphe talaphe / prakarṣaṇi svāhā</s> //

children.text: kṣipraṃ saṃtiṣṭhatāṃ garbhaḥ samyag vardhantu indriyā /
children.translated_text: May the embryo quickly become established, may the senses develop properly;

children.text: garbhasthāḥ sukhino bhontu mā ca naśyantu jātakāḥ //
children.translated_text: may those dwelling in the womb be happy, and may the newborn not perish.
May the embryo remain healthy and be delivered in due time;
with various colored threads, unbroken rice, and white mustard seeds—

children.text: eṣā rakṣā samākhyātā ciraṃ jīvantu dārakāḥ /
children.translated_text: this protection has been proclaimed; may children live long!

children.text: tato 'tha śāstā sarvajña imāṃ gāthām udāharet //
children.translated_text: Then the Teacher, the Omniscient One, uttered this verse:

body.text: rakṣito bhavantu garbhaḥ sukhaṃ modantu dārakāḥ /
body.translated_text: May the womb be protected, may the children rejoice in happiness!

body.text: syād yathedaṃ /
body.translated_text: It is as follows:

body.text: bodhi bodhi / mahābodhi / bodhānumate / phalini / bahuphale / śikṣe / śikṣāsāravate / sāgale / durāsade / dūrāgame / śūraprāpte / śūravate / bhage / bhagābhage / bhagini / nivāriṇi svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>bodhi bodhi / mahābodhi / bodhānumate / phalini / bahuphale / śikṣe / śikṣāsāravate / sāgale / durāsade / dūrāgame / śūraprāpte / śūravate / bhage / bhagābhage / bhagini / nivāriṇi svāhā</s> //

children.translated_text: Then the fifteen <s>grahāḥ</s> (seizers), who always feed on blood,
having paid homage with palms joined, spoke to the Protector of the World:

children.text: yatredaṃ nagare sūtraṃ grāme vā yadi vā gṛhe /
children.translated_text: "Wherever this <s>sūtra</s> abides in a city, or in a village, or in a house,

children.text: nātra bālā mariṣyanti yatra tiṣṭhet subhāṣitaṃ //
children.translated_text: no children shall die there, wherever this well-spoken teaching remains.

body.text: anuvṛṣṭyā bhajiṣyāmo yathā tava mahāmuni /
body.translated_text: We shall serve you with constant devotion, O great sage!

body.text: namo bhagavate buddhāya namo brahmaṇe sidhyantu //
body.translated_text: <s>namo bhagavate buddhāya namo brahmaṇe sidhyantu</s> //

body.text: mantrapadās tārayantu imāṃ vidyāṃ brahmā manyatu svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>mantrapadās tārayantu imāṃ vidyāṃ brahmā manyatu svāhā</s> //

body.text: atha vaiśramaṇo mahārāja ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā kṛtāñjalir
body.translated_text: Then <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, the Great King, having arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, with palms joined,

body.text: bhagavantaṃ namasyamāno 'vocat /
body.translated_text: bowing to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke:

body.text: yaḥ kaścid bhadanta bhagavan śrāvaka idaṃ mahāsāhasrapramardanīsūtram udgṛhṇayād vārayed vācayed deśayet paryavāpnuyāt tena vā bahuśrutena yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / caityapūjā pareṇa bhavitavyam / aṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ ca tv ete yakṣasyodāracaityapūjāṃ kṛtvā vidyā āvartayitavyā / tasyāṣṭamyāṃ catvāro rājapuruṣā mahārājānāṃ purataḥ samanvāharanti nāma codghoṣayanti / caturdaśyāṃ caturṇāṃ mahārājānāṃ purataḥ samanvāharanti nāma codghoṣayanti / pañcadaśyāṃ svayam eva catvāro mahārājānaḥ samanvāharanti nāma codghoṣayanti //
body.translated_text: "Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, whatever <s>śrāvaka</s> (disciple) should learn, master, recite, teach, or fully comprehend this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī-sūtra</s>, that learned one should practice <s>yoga</s> (meditation). One must perform <s>caityapūjā</s> (worship at a shrine). On the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days, having performed a splendid <s>caityapūjā</s> for the <s>yakṣa</s>, the <s>vidyā</s> (spell) should be recited. On the eighth day, four royal officers convey and proclaim the names before the Great Kings. On the fourteenth day, they convey and proclaim the names before the four Great Kings. On the fifteenth day, the four Great Kings themselves convey and proclaim the names.

body.text: sarvasatvahitānukaṃpīvatāyaṃ bhagavataḥ śrāvako ya idaṃ mahāsāhasrapramardanīsūtram udgṛhṇati dhārayati vācayati paryavāpnoti / tasya ca bhadanta bhagavan vayaṃ catvāro mahārājānaś cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair autsukyaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ / satkṛtaś ca bhaviṣyati / sarvasatvair gurukṛtaś ca mānitaś ca pūjitaś ca rājñāṃ rājamahāmātrāṇāṃ ca bhaviṣyati / anyatīrthakaśravaṇabrāhmaṇaparivrājakānāṃ pūjyo bhaviṣyati mitrāmitramadhyagato 'pi satkṛto bhaviṣyati / te ca śrāddhena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā śucinā bhavitavyam / śucikāyena śucivastrābharaṇaśayanopakaraṇaviśeṣeṇa / na kudeśalābhena na kumitrasaṃsargeṇa na kudeśavāsasaṃprayuktena bhavitavyam / yasya ca bhūtagrahagṛhītasya purata idaṃ mahāsāhasrapramardanī nāma sūtraṃ śrāvayiṣyati / tasya catvāro mahārājānaḥ svayam eva rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ saṃvidhāsyanti / evaṃ maharddhikaṃ bhadanta bhagavan mahāsāhasrapramardanīsūtraṃ yasyāpi gṛhe ekam api rātriṃ divaṃ vāsaṃ kalpayiṣyati / tasya saṃvatsaraṃ yāvad amanuṣyā avatāraṃ na lapsyanti / namasyanīyaś ca bhaviṣyati sarvabhūtagaṇasya yaḥ idaṃ mahāsāhasrapramardanīsūtraṃ dhārayiṣyati / tasya kāṅkṣataś catvāro mahārājāno sukham upadarśayanti / kimaṅga punar itare yakṣarākṣasāḥ / tat kasya hetor ye kecil loke vidyā
body.translated_text: Out of compassion for the welfare of all beings, the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>śrāvaka</s> who learns, retains, recites, and fully comprehends this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī-sūtra</s> — for him, venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, we the four Great Kings shall provide robes, almsfood, bedding, and medicines for the sick with eager care. He shall be honored by all beings, revered, respected, and worshipped. He shall be honored by kings and royal ministers. He shall be worthy of worship by other sectarians, ascetics, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and wanderers. Even when among friends, enemies, and neutrals, he shall be honored. That faithful son or daughter of good family must be pure — pure in body, with pure garments, ornaments, and excellent bedding. One must not resort to unwholesome places, nor associate with bad companions, nor dwell in unwholesome regions. Before one who is seized by a <s>bhūtagraha</s> (spirit-seizure), when this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī</s> <s>sūtra</s> is recited, the four Great Kings themselves shall arrange protection, shielding, and guardianship. So powerful is this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī-sūtra</s>, venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, that in whatever house it resides even for a single night or day, for a full year non-human beings shall find no entry. And whoever holds this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī-sūtra</s> shall be worthy of homage by all hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits). For one who desires it, the four Great Kings shall reveal happiness. How much more so for other <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>! For what reason? Whatever <s>vidyās</s> (spells) in the world

body.text: saṃvidhāsyanti / satvānāṃ hitāya / imāni mantrapadāni tebhyo varapravaraśreṣṭhaviśiṣṭottamāni / gaṃbhīravipulo pramāṇāni dūrāvataraṇā asādhāraṇā iyaṃ dharmamudrā //
body.translated_text: they shall arrange for the benefit of beings — these <s>mantrapadāni</s> (sacred words) are the most excellent, supreme, distinguished, and unsurpassed among them. Profound and vast in measure, difficult to fathom, incomparable — this is the <s>dharmamudrā</s> (seal of the Dharma)."

children.translated_text: Then <s>Indra</s>, the thousand-eyed king of the gods, lord of <s>Śacī</s>,
standing with palms joined and having paid homage, spoke to the Protector of the World:
"Well-spoken is this <s>vidyā</s>, which brings welfare to all worlds.
I shall proclaim a <s>vidyā</s> combined with <s>mantra</s>-medicines.
<s>Śirīṣa</s> (silk-tree) flowers, <s>apāmārga</s> (prickly chaff-flower), <s>agaru</s> (aloe wood), <s>kaṭaka</s>-fruit,
<s>śaileya</s> (rock lichen), <s>eḍa</s> (a plant), <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (Indian madder), <s>sūkarī</s>, <s>markaṭī</s>, <s>jayā</s> (a plant),

children.text: paripelavaṃ rasaṃ vīrā sāmakaṃ tagaraṃ busā /
children.translated_text: <s>paripelava</s>, juice, <s>vīrā</s>, <s>sāmaka</s> (a millet), <s>tagara</s> (valerian), <s>busā</s> (chaff),
sandalwood paste, <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus root), nail-shaped <s>patraka</s> (leaf spice), and <s>varā</s> (Terminalia chebula),

children.text: priyaṃgu rocanā spṛkkā sarṣapāś ca manaḥśilāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>priyaṅgu</s> (beauty-berry), <s>rocanā</s> (yellow orpiment), <s>spṛkkā</s> (a fragrant plant), mustard seeds, and <s>manaḥśilā</s> (realgar),
bark, saffron, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), combined with <s>patra</s> (bay leaf) coloring.
A preparation compounded from these releases all <s>grahāḥ</s> (seizers).
For all afflictions caused by <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), this is known as a collyrium for the eyes.
Those who are seized are freed by it, as if struck by the thunderbolt-arrows of spirits.
It should be applied to great trees and likewise to great <s>caityas</s> (shrines).

children.text: yo hi paśyati tat sthānaṃ bhūtebhyo na bhayaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever sees that place shall have no fear from <s>bhūtas</s>.

children.text: sthānaṃ na tatra bhūtānāṃ nānyeṣām ahitaiṣiṇām //
children.translated_text: There is no abode there for <s>bhūtas</s>, nor for any other malevolent beings.
It should also be applied to drums, conch shells, <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, and <s>paṇavas</s> (kettledrums).
As far as the sound is heard, the hosts of <s>bhūtas</s> tremble.
One may also apply it to <s>yakṣa</s>-figures and to village-roaming birds.

children.text: yatrāsau vrajate pakṣī diśaṃ cāpi digantaram //
children.translated_text: Wherever that bird flies, to any direction or horizon,

children.text: sthānaṃ na tatra bhūtānāṃ nānyeṣām ahitaiṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: there is no abode there for <s>bhūtas</s>, nor for any other malevolent beings.
It should be cast into rivers, streams, and ponds, here and there.

children.text: samantād yojanaṃ tatra svasti śāntir bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: For a <s>yojana</s> (league) all around, there shall be well-being and peace.
Even in attacks by weapons and encounters with enemy armies,
it should be applied to all vital points — one shall emerge safely.
For goiters, hemorrhoids, herpes, and boils,

body.text: viṣadaṣṭe viṣapīte pītvā kṣipraṃ pramucyate /
body.translated_text: for one bitten by poison or who has drunk poison, drinking it one is swiftly freed.

body.text: etena lepayed gātraṃ sarvakākhordacchedanam //
body.translated_text: One should anoint the limbs with this — it cuts away all <s>kākhordas</s> (sorceries).

children.translated_text: It is proven effective for prevailing in disputes and for release from the king's gate (prison).
The unsuccessful attains success; the powerless attains sovereignty.

children.text: aputro labhate putram adhano labhate dhanam /
children.translated_text: The sonless obtains a son; the poor obtains wealth.
It accomplishes <s>mantras</s> equal to the realm of the <s>vidyādharas</s> (spell-bearers).

children.text: tiryagyonigate caiva tat syād vṛkṣaphaleṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Even for beings in animal rebirths, it works upon the fruits of trees.
For the wise <s>vidyādhara</s>, it brings peace and auspiciousness.

body.text: tatra mantrapadāny asti indrasya vacanaṃ yathā /
body.translated_text: Here are the <s>mantrapadāni</s> (sacred words), as spoken by <s>Indra</s>:

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: It is as follows:

body.text: akrame / vikrame / bhūtaghoṣe / bhūtaṃgame / dahani / dhadhare / dharadhare / dadhini / nikhume / khukhume / khakha khakha / sāraṃgame / candre / capale / halime / hale hariṇi svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>akrame / vikrame / bhūtaghoṣe / bhūtaṃgame / dahani / dhadhare / dharadhare / dadhini / nikhume / khukhume / khakha khakha / sāraṃgame / candre / capale / halime / hale hariṇi svāhā</s> //

body.text: svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvadigvidigbhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca sarvadigvidigbhyaḥ svāhā</s> //

body.text: nihatāḥ sarvapāpāni svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>nihatāḥ sarvapāpāni svāhā</s> //

children.text: tato brahmā ca śakraś ca lokapālā maheśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, the world-protectors, <s>Maheśvara</s>,
all the <s>yakṣa</s>-generals, and <s>Hārītī</s> together with her children,
with one voice, in one tone, spoke with palms joined:
"Radiant as a thousand suns, luminous as the full moon,

children.text: sadevamānuṣe loke sadṛśas te na vidyate /
children.translated_text: in the world of gods and humans, none is equal to you.
Inconceivable and well-applied is this crusher of <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>,
the <s>vidyā</s> named 'Releaser of Kings,' protector through dispassion,
the one named <s>Sāhasrapramardanī</s>, auspicious in arising, supreme among Great Kings,
victorious in battle and warfare, crusher of all enemies,
the supreme <s>sūtra</s> for protection in the great thousandfold world."

children.text: namas te puruṣavīra namas te puruṣottama /
children.translated_text: "Homage to you, O heroic man! Homage to you, O supreme among men!"
Having paid homage with palms joined, they vanished right there.

body.text: atha bhagavān sāyāhnakālasamaye pratisaṃlayanād utthāya bhikṣūn āmantrayāmāsa /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at the time of evening, rising from meditation, addressed the monks:

body.text: udgṛhṇadhvaṃ bhikṣavo mahāsāhasrapramardanīśūtraṃ dhārayata vācayata paryavāpnuyāt / tad bhaviṣyati / sadevakasya lokasya
body.translated_text: "Learn, O monks, the <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī-sūtra</s>! Retain it, recite it, and fully comprehend it! It shall be for the benefit of the world together with its gods,

body.text: dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya sparśavihāratāyai / yaḥ kaścid bhikṣavo mama śravaka etena mahāsāhasrapramardanīsūtreṇa śuṣkavṛkṣasyāpi paritrāṇaṃ badhnīyāt parigrahaṃ tasya patrapuṣpaphalāni jayeran / kimaṅga punaḥ savijñānasya kāyasyānyatra pūrvakarmavipākena //
body.translated_text: for the long-lasting welfare, benefit, happiness, and comfortable dwelling of all. O monks, whatever disciple of mine should bind a protection even for a withered tree by means of this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī-sūtra</s>, leaves, flowers, and fruits would spring forth for that tree. How much more so for a body endowed with consciousness — unless prevented by the ripening of former <s>karma</s>!"

body.text: evam uktās te bhikṣavo bhagavantam etad avocat /
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, those monks spoke to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: yānīmāni bhadanta bhagavan pañcamahārakṣāsūtrāṇi bhāṣitāni / syād yathedam / mahāsāhasrapramardanī / mahāmāyūrī mahāśītavatī mahāpratisarā mahāmantrānusāraṇī ceti / tāni ca bhagavatā pañcāmiṣaparivarjinenānujñatāni vācayitavyāni / piṇḍapātraṃ ca bhojanaṃ niśrāya pravrajyā vyākṛtā / alpaṃ ca bhagavan piṇḍapātraṃ pañcāmiṣaparivarjitam / idam eva bahutaraṃ yad idaṃ pañcāmiṣasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ tatra vayaṃ bhagavan kathaṃ pratipadyāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: "Venerable <s>Bhagavān</s>, these five great protective <s>sūtras</s> have been spoken, namely: <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī</s>, <s>Mahāmāyūrī</s>, <s>Mahāśītavatī</s>, <s>Mahāpratisarā</s>, and <s>Mahāmantrānusāraṇī</s>. These have been authorized by the <s>Bhagavān</s> to be recited while abstaining from the five impure foods. And the going forth has been declared to depend on almsfood. But, <s>Bhagavān</s>, almsfood free of the five impure substances is scarce, while that which is mixed with the five impure substances is far more abundant. How then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, should we proceed?"

body.text: evam ukte bhagavān tān bhikṣūn etad avocat /
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke to those monks:

body.text: tena hi bhikṣavo yo hy etat mahāsāhasrapramardanīsūtraṃ dhārayitavyam / tenākṣateyaṃ dhāraṇī ātmarakṣāyai dhārayitavyā / tena hi piṇḍapātraṃ parigṛhītā āhāre pratikūlasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / pañcāmiṣasaṃsṛṣṭapiṇḍapātre pañcāmiṣaparivarjitasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / sarvasaṃskṛte anityasaṃjñā / anitye duḥkhasaṃjñā / duḥkhe anātmasaṃjñā / anātmany aśubhasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / kutaḥ pañcāmiṣāṇi kasya vā pañcāmiṣāṇi / ko vā pañcāmiṣāṇi paribhojyante / nāsti satvaḥ kutaḥ satvaḥ / sa satvo nopalabhyate / tatra cāhāra pañcāmiṣāsaṃsṛṣṭasaṃjñakaraṇīyā / ātmarakṣā aṣṭamyāṃ caturdaśyāṃ pañcadaśyāṃ ca rājagotrāya kanyāya susnātāya subhūṣitāya ahorātro vapuṣṭāya pañcaśikṣāpadaparigṛhītayā lohitaṃ sūtraṃ caturguṇaṃ kārayitvā mantradhāreṇa vidyā smarayitavyā / granthiṃ kṛtvā tat sūtraṃ navena śastreṇa cchitvā dagdhā ratnabhaṇḍo vā udakaparipūrṇaṃ kṛtvā puṣpair ācchādayitvā nānāgandhena dhūpayitvā iyaṃ vidyā āvartayitavyā / yāvat taj jātaṃ sūtraṃ bhājane prādurbhavati / tac ca pāṇau bandhayitvā vācyam //
body.translated_text: "Therefore, monks, whoever would hold this <s>Mahāsāhasrapramardanī-sūtra</s>, he should hold this <s>dhāraṇī</s> with intact syllables for self-protection. He should generate the perception of repulsiveness toward food when receiving almsfood. When almsfood is mixed with the five impure substances, he should generate the perception of it being free from the five impure substances. Toward all conditioned things, the perception of impermanence; toward the impermanent, the perception of suffering; toward suffering, the perception of non-self; toward non-self, the perception of the impure — these should be generated. Whence are the five impure substances? Whose are the five impure substances? Who consumes the five impure substances? There is no being — whence a being? That being is not found. Therefore, regarding food, one should produce the perception of it being unmixed with the five impure substances. For self-protection, on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth days, a girl of royal lineage, well-bathed and well-adorned, who has observed a day and night of fasting and has taken the five precepts, should make a red thread fourfold, and the <s>mantra</s>-holder should recite the <s>vidyā</s>. Having tied a knot, that thread should be cut with a new blade, burned, and placed in a jeweled vessel or one filled with water. Having covered it with flowers and fumigated it with various fragrances, this <s>vidyā</s> should be recited until that knotted thread reappears in the vessel. Then, having bound it on the hand, one should recite:

children.translated_text: "By the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who deceived him, to <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the Śākyas), the Protector,
poisoned food was offered by <s>Girigupta</s>.
The Teacher, having accepted it, rendered the food non-poisonous for the diners.
By this truthful utterance, may the food become <s>amṛta</s> (ambrosia)!
The deities of <s>Vipaśyin</s>, of <s>Śikhin</s>, and likewise of <s>Viśvabhu</s>,
the great and powerful ones devoted to <s>Krakucchanda</s> and his deity,
the <s>Indras</s> of the god named <s>Kanaka</s>, and of the glorious <s>Kāśyapa</s>,
the devoted ones of <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the lords of the thirty-three gods —
the four world-protectors, <s>Māṇibhadra</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>,
the <s>rākṣasī</s> <s>Mahākālī</s>, and likewise <s>Caṇḍacaṇḍālinī</s> —

children.text: idaṃ puṣpaṃ ca gandhaṃ ca pratigṛhṇantu mamāhutim /
children.translated_text: may they accept this flower and fragrance and my oblation!

children.text: prīṇitā pūjitā bhūtvā ete śodhantu bhojanam //
children.translated_text: Being pleased and worshipped, may they purify the food!
That which is mixed with the five impure substances — may they make it unmixed for me!
May I eat all food free from the five impure substances!
The earth's essences are the foundation of all seed-groups;
may all food that is mixed become unmixed for me!

children.text: chinnaṃ dagdhaṃ yathā sūtraṃ tādṛśaṃ bhavate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a thread that has been cut and burned becomes as it was before,
so may they make that which is mixed with food unmixed for me!"

body.text: syād yathedam /
body.translated_text: It is as follows:

body.text: khakhame / khakha khakha / khukhume / sime sime / sihune / simi sime / svasti svasti svasti svasti / śānti śānti sārāgri / pañcāmiṣeṇa saṃsṛṣṭaṃ yathā hāra nirāmiṣam / yena dagdhaṃ yathā sūtraṃ satyaṃ kurvantu tādṛśam //
body.translated_text: <s>khakhame / khakha khakha / khukhume / sime sime / sihune / simi sime / svasti svasti svasti svasti / śānti śānti sārāgri / pañcāmiṣeṇa saṃsṛṣṭaṃ yathā hāra nirāmiṣam / yena dagdhaṃ yathā sūtraṃ satyaṃ kurvantu tādṛśam</s> //

body.text: syād yathedam //
body.translated_text: It is as follows:

body.text: kalake / kalale / balanikaruṇalāye / khalume / agnisaṃkrāmani svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>kalake / kalale / balanikaruṇalāye / khalume / agnisaṃkrāmani svāhā</s> //

body.text: vipaśyibuddhaṃ śaraṇam upaimi / śikhinaṃ ca buddhaṃ sugataṃ ca viśvabhum / krakucchandabuddhaṃ kanakamuniṃ ca kāśyapam / viśāradaṃ śakyamuniṃ ca gautamam / etena saptān narottamānāṃ puṣpaiś ca gandhaiś ca śarīrapūjāṃ kāyena vācā
body.translated_text: I go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Vipaśyin</s>; to the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Śikhin</s> and the <s>Sugata</s> <s>Viśvabhu</s>; to the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Krakucchanda</s>, <s>Kanakamuni</s>, and <s>Kāśyapa</s>; to the Confident One, <s>Śākyamuni Gautama</s>. With flowers, fragrances, and worship of the bodies of these seven supreme among men, with body, speech,

body.text: manasā ca kṛtvā prasannacittaśaraṇaṃ hy upaimi / eteṣu buddheṣu maharddhikeṣu yā devatāḥ santi abhiprasannāḥ / tā devatā āttamanā udagrāḥ kurvanti śāntiṃ ca nityam / svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca svāhā //
body.translated_text: and mind — having made these offerings with a clear heart, I go for refuge. May the deities who are devoted to these <s>Buddhas</s> of great power — may those deities, joyful and exalted, always bring about peace! <s>svasty astu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca svāhā</s> //

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanās te ca bhikṣavo bodhisatvā sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Delighted, those monks, the <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and that entire assembly together with the gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words.

body.text: āryamahāsāhasrapramardanī nama mahāyānasūtraṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Āryamahāsāhasrapramardanī</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s>, is complete.
